text: \Title{Gene-level concordance amid divergent mean polyadenylation-site shifts during reprogramming}

% Structured abstract: one paragraph, no subheadings, about 200 words maximum. % Required information logic: Background -> Methods -> Results -> Conclusion. \abstract{Alternative polyadenylation (APA) reshapes transcript $3'$ ends during somatic cell reprogramming, but the extent of gene-level recurrence across defined state comparisons and species remains unresolved. We assembled 551,201 human and mouse cells from seven single-cell studies and summarized each gene's polyadenylation site (PAS) usage with a distance-weighted PAS usage index (DWUI). The mean direction of PAS shifts differed between systems, and pluripotency-acquiring cells retained only part of the intermediate-state shifts. Within each species, independent studies shifted the same genes in the same direction more often than expected (510 human and 488 mouse genes against 373 expected each), an excess robust to measurement and background controls. Of 200 measurable mouse genes recurrent against an alternative mesenchymal state, 97 also met the same criterion against the somatic source in both studies. Sharing between human and mouse was weak. In candidate transcript intervals, PAS usage changes altered the retention of predicted miRNA and RNA-binding protein sites. In \textit{Rad23b}, pluripotency-acquiring cells of both mouse studies included less of an interval carrying a miR-290/302-compatible seed than mesenchymal cells did, a structure also present in public long-read transcript models. Reprogramming-associated APA combines system-specific mean shifts with selective gene-level recurrence and yields testable sequence-resolved candidates.}
\keyword{alternative polyadenylation; somatic cell reprogramming; single-cell RNA sequencing; PAS usage; cross-study concordance; cross-species comparison}

Alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a regulatory layer well suited to this question. By selecting among polyadenylation sites (PASs), APA produces transcripts with different $3'$ ends, which can change the $3'$ untranslated region ($3'$ UTR) or the coding sequence. The resulting isoforms can differ in stability, localization, translation and recognition by microRNAs (miRNAs) or RNA-binding proteins (RBPs)\citep{TianManley2017,MitschkaMayr2022,TianYuZhang2026,Berkovits2015}. PAS choice at individual genes can depart both from the global balance of proximal and distal shifts and from changes in gene expression, so APA offers information beyond expression profiles\citep{Sandberg2008,Ji2009Development,Shulman2019,Agarwal2021,Fansler2024}.

APA changes during reprogramming. Bulk analyses reported source-dependent $3'$ UTR shortening during somatic cell reprogramming, lengthening during spermatogonial-cell reprogramming and higher-than-random agreement among data sets\citep{JiTian2009}. SCAPE later resolved non-monotonic PAS dynamics within a mouse time course\citep{Zhou2022SCAPE}, long-read sequencing traced isoform switching during reprogramming and showed that a switch between isoforms of the long non-coding RNA \textit{Snhg26} promotes pluripotency acquisition\citep{Fort2026LongRead}, and the APA regulators NUDT21, Fip1 and TDP-43 have been linked to reprogramming or pluripotency\citep{Brumbaugh2018,Lackford2014,Modic2019}. Single-cell data now cover many reprogramming systems, but how far gene-level APA responses recur among them, under explicit state comparisons and between species, remains undefined.

Defining it requires comparing like with like. Studies sample different states, so a gene can appear to change only because the reference differs. Comparing pluripotency-acquiring cells with their somatic source asks a different biological question from comparing them with an alternative state captured in the same culture. Intermediate states can also carry changes that disappear by the endpoint. A change in PAS usage proportions can produce a large or a small net shift in position. A net-position summary keeps the direction of that shift and a redistribution summary keeps the size of the proportion change, so the two are complementary. Locating the sequence that a transcript gains or loses further requires analysis of transcript intervals.

Here we assembled a single-cell atlas of 551,201 human and mouse cells from seven reprogramming studies and compared PAS usage between defined states within and across studies. The mean direction of PAS shifts differed among systems, and pluripotency-acquiring states retained only part of the shifts observed in intermediate states. Within each species, however, independent studies shifted the same genes in the same direction more often than expected, whereas sharing between human and mouse was weak. At the transcript level, PAS usage changes altered the retention of predicted miRNA and RBP sites in candidate intervals. Candidate RBP expression and public long-read isoform structures placed these changes in context and yielded testable gene--interval--factor relationships.
\subsection{Mean DWUI shifts differ across reprogramming systems}

We first asked whether reprogramming moves PAS usage in a shared direction. The seven 10x Genomics $3'$ single-cell studies analyzed here, four in human and three in mouse, together comprised 551,201 cells. Within each study we resolved local expression states, 111 in total, and grouped them into 14 display families along seven supported routes (Fig.~\ref{fig:reprogramming-overview}A,B and Supplementary Table~S4). Five families anchor the comparisons that follow: source-like or fibroblast (S), source-exit or remodeling (R), epithelial or mixed-transition (E), pluripotency-acquisition (P), and mesenchymal or extracellular-matrix-retaining (M) states (Supplementary Figs.~S1--S3 and Table~S5). M is an alternative state sampled alongside P and serves as a parallel comparator. The labels align broad state categories across studies.

PASs were identified from read-end coverage within each study. Each gene's PAS usage was then summarized with the distance-weighted PAS usage index (DWUI), the usage-weighted position of its PASs on a study-specific, strand-oriented axis running from proximal (0) to distal (1). A negative change therefore denotes a proximal shift and a positive change a distal shift. Independent annotations supported the PAS catalog. Between 72.7\% and 96.3\% of coordinate-evaluable primary PASs lay within 50 nt of an external reference site, and in sequence-matched subsets canonical upstream polyadenylation signals occurred at 15.8\%--33.7\% of candidate PASs, compared with 2.6\%--4.8\% of control sequences (Supplementary Fig.~S4A,B). \Reserved{SCAPE-APA and polyApipe re-analysis of the same reads: completed scope, site agreement, coverage and effect agreement on native and common measurement layers, each with its denominator (Supplementary Fig.~S5A--D)}.

Mean PAS position moved in opposite directions in different systems. Relative to the S cells observed in each study, human Xing2020 shifted toward distal PASs across E, P and M, whereas mouse Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i shifted toward proximal PASs, most strongly in E and P (Fig.~\ref{fig:reprogramming-overview}C,D). The other routes showed smaller or mixed changes. The opposition held in several fixed-background sensitivity analyses, although weaker means remained sensitive to the reference and to the measurable gene background. Against documented pre-induction sources, the mean DWUI change in P was $+0.0286$ in Xing2020 and $-0.0091$ in Guo2019--CIP. On a common-contributor background, all six PAS counting rules kept Xing2020 and Guan2022--0618 positive and both mouse series negative, and only the smaller Guan2022--0809 shift crossed zero. Restricting genes to common contributors changed the means, by up to $-0.0199$ in Schiebinger2019--2i ($-0.0066$ to $-0.0265$), but reversed none of these four directions (Fig.~\ref{fig:reprogramming-overview}D). Medians, proximal-to-distal event balances and 710 common orthologs gave the same directions (Supplementary Fig.~S6A,B). The mean was most sensitive in Schiebinger2019--2i, where its two D0 sources gave $-0.00156$ and $+0.01100$ on the same 1,912 genes while medians and event balances stayed proximal (Supplementary Fig.~S6A,D).

The difference also held on a physical scale. Within annotation-compatible tandem $3'$ UTRs, mean nucleotide-weighted shifts were $+56.9$ nt in Xing2020, $-19.4$ nt in Guo2019--CIP and $-62.2$ nt in Schiebinger2019--2i (809, 788 and 750 genes; Supplementary Fig.~S6E). Net PAS change therefore had a system-specific direction, both on the relative DWUI scale and in nucleotides within tandem $3'$ UTRs. A mean can also hide changes that differ between genes and between states, and we next followed individual genes through the intermediate states of each route.
\subsection{State-resolved DWUI profiles distinguish endpoint-retained and transient remodeling}

Along the S--R--E--P sequence, gene-level DWUI profiles took three characteristic forms. We selected genes whose state-resolved profiles were measurable and correlated between studies, 540 in mouse and 897 in human, and clustered them jointly by species-balanced $k$-means at $k=3$. The classes corresponded to proximal accumulation toward P (C1), early distal displacement followed by reversal (C2), and distal remodeling that strengthened at later states (C3) (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-dynamic-architecture}A). Mouse genes concentrated in C1 (314/540) and human genes in C3 (517/897), in line with the mean direction in each species. Because the genes were selected for cross-study similarity, these frequencies describe the selected cohort only. The class patterns were stable to the perturbations in Supplementary Fig.~S7A--C.

C2 genes had largely returned toward their source position by P. To quantify this, we compared the total distance travelled across the four states, the path length $L=|R-S|+|E-R|+|P-E|$, with the net endpoint displacement $D=|P-S|$ in 1,977 complete gene--route profiles. Median $D/L$ was 0.836 in C1, 0.234 in C2 and 0.609 in C3. A typical C2 gene therefore kept less than a quarter of its path at P, a median transient fraction $T=1-D/L$ of 0.766 (route medians 0.743--0.813; Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-dynamic-architecture}B,C and Supplementary Fig.~S7D--F). Decomposing each path into adjacent-state steps located the C2 reversal and the late C3 accentuation along each route (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-dynamic-architecture}C). Monotone change with measurement error produced much smaller reversals. When each gene was simulated to move monotonically between its observed endpoints, with empirical metacell errors added and gene selection and clustering repeated, the corresponding class had a median $T$ of 0 and route-specific 97.5th percentiles of 0.173--0.358 (Supplementary Fig.~S7G,H). Endpoint contrasts therefore capture only part of the net PAS-position variation observed across the sampled states. Systematic differences between states, which the model leaves out, could also contribute.

PAS trajectories followed expression trajectories only in part. DWUI profiles were locally organized on the expression embedding, and part of this organization remained after adjustment for state and coverage (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-dynamic-architecture}D and Supplementary Fig.~S8A,B). For individual genes, however, DWUI and gene expression (GEX) profiles were weakly correlated, with medians of 0.161 in mouse and 0.025 in human across all gene--route profiles of the three routes per species, and these pooled values hid opposite signs between classes. In the three routes with complete S--R--E--P profiles, correlations were positive in C1 (0.501, 0.295 and 0.407 in Schiebinger2019--2i, Guo2019--CIP and Xing2020), near zero or negative in C2 ($-0.017$, 0.060 and $-0.300$) and negative in C3 ($-0.173$, $-0.290$ and $-0.316$), whereas the other three routes showed different orderings (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-dynamic-architecture}E). Between adjacent states, DWUI and GEX changes shared the same nonzero sign in only 50.9\% of mouse and 46.6\% of human transitions (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-dynamic-architecture}F and Supplementary Fig.~S8C--F). PAS usage and expression therefore changed with little coordination between adjacent states. Intermediate states were sampled unevenly across studies and align less finely than endpoints. We therefore turned to the net changes that separate P from its reference states and asked whether independent studies show them in the same genes.
\subsection{Gene-level APA responses show excess same-direction concordance within species}

Despite the divergent mean trends, individual genes shifted PAS usage in the same direction in independent studies of the same species. We compared P with two reference states. The documented-source contrast (P--S) asks how P differs from the somatic cells that were reprogrammed. It was available in two studies per species, Xing2020 and Guan2022 in human and Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i in mouse. The paired contrast with the alternative M state (P--M) compares cells captured in the same physical libraries and was available in three human and two mouse studies. A gene showed same-direction recurrence when it shifted by $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.02$ in the same direction in at least two studies, and we refer to such genes as recurrent. Their numbers were compared with permutations matched for expression, APA coverage, PAS number and reference DWUI. P--S identified 510 recurrent genes in human and 488 in mouse, against a permutation median of 373 in each species. P--M identified 170 and 216, against 97 and 121 (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}A). The excess also held at the stronger 0.05 threshold, and all eight tests reached the permutation floor ($q\leq1.0\times10^{-4}$; Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}A).

This excess was a property of the gene set and was robust to the removal of marginal calls. It remained when each gene's within-library bootstrap interval had to exclude zero, which retained 465 of the 510 human and 463 of the 488 mouse P--S genes, and under 20-UMI thinning, cell-cycle matching, a common PAS axis and six-rule counting consensus (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}B, Supplementary Fig.~S9A,C and Tables~S18 and S22). Nested backgrounds that progressively fixed the number of measuring studies, expression and coverage, baseline PAS position and PAS number kept the expected P--S counts between 353 and 375 in human and between 362 and 373 in mouse, and all 40 tests retained support (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}B and Supplementary Fig.~S9D). Measurement noise alone produced far fewer recurrent genes: random halves of a single state yielded median counts of 7 in human and 17 in mouse, against 367 and 250 for P--S on the same measurable backgrounds (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}B).

Support was weaker for individual genes than for the set. On the common axis only 289 of the 510 human and 327 of the 488 mouse genes kept their identity and direction (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}B), and within-state noise reached 0.0265--0.0406 in absolute DWUI at the 95th percentile. The 0.02 threshold therefore marks candidate responses, and single genes require further support. Inference with culture wells as units, within the existing Schiebinger2019--2i data, covered only part of the candidates: 62 of the 216 recurrent mouse P--M genes had sufficient coverage in replicate wells across collection dates. All 62 retained same-direction support ($q<0.05$) and 60 retained the 0.02 effect (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}B and Supplementary Fig.~S10C). These wells derive from one cell line, so they show repeatability within that line. \Reserved{support for the original recurrent lists under SCAPE-APA and polyApipe, kept separate from cross-study recurrence (Supplementary Fig.~S5E,F and Table~S30)}. As a separate, descriptive check of direction, a public PAS-seq data set from mouse embryonic fibroblasts and iPSCs agreed for 19 of 20 and 5 of 6 measurable counting-rule consensus genes from Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i, small and overlapping subsets (Supplementary Table~S23). None of these analyses removes the limitations of sparse source replication or of the differences in date and medium between source and P states.

What a recurrent gene represents depends on the reference state. When the 216 mouse P--M genes were re-measured with common P, M and S contributors, 200 remained measurable. Of these, 97 shifted in their P--M direction by at least 0.02 against both M and the documented source in both studies. Within Xing2020 alone, 78 of 146 measurable human genes met the same criterion against both references (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}C). These dual-reference genes mark P relative to both references. \textit{Slc38a2} is one of them. P used more proximal PASs than either S or M in both mouse studies, with P--S and P--M effects of $-0.0263$ and $-0.0769$ in Guo2019--CIP and $-0.0794$ and $-0.0335$ in Schiebinger2019--2i (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}D). Both studies thus shared an ordering in which P was more proximal than both S and M, whereas M differed from S in opposite directions.

Which genes counted as recurrent also depended on how PAS usage was summarized. DWUI records net position. Maximum proportion redistribution (MPRO), the range of site-level usage differences, records redistribution among PASs regardless of direction, and the rank-weighted usage index (RWUI) offers a directional alternative to DWUI (Supplementary Fig.~S6F--H). Each summary showed excess recurrence within species (all 24 tests $q\leq2.0\times10^{-4}$; Supplementary Fig.~S11A), but they selected partly different genes. At an MPRO threshold of 0.10, P--M added 82 mouse and 70 human genes outside the DWUI sets, and 60 of 74 completely measured mouse additions also passed this threshold against the source in both studies (Supplementary Fig.~S11A,B and Table~S20A). \textit{Nudt21}, whose depletion enhances reprogramming\citep{Brumbaugh2018}, shows how the summaries diverge. Against M, it shifted proximally in both mouse studies ($\Delta$DWUI $-0.0868$ and $-0.0692$). Against the source, its net shifts were small ($-0.0194$ and $-0.0167$), yet its PAS usage was strongly redistributed in Schiebinger2019--2i (MPRO 0.4630, compared with 0.0404 in Guo2019--CIP; Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}E and Supplementary Table~S20B). \textit{Slc38a2} shows the converse, with recurrent net shifts but a Schiebinger2019--2i MPRO of 0.0643, below 0.10 (Supplementary Table~S21A). The two summaries thus capture complementary aspects of the same PAS usage measurements.

At the endpoints, as along the trajectories, PAS usage carried information beyond expression. Among genes with recurrent P--S DWUI responses at 0.02, 65 in mouse and 78 in human changed expression in opposite directions in the two studies. In human, such genes were more frequent than expected when response identity was permuted ($q=0.0032$). Mouse counts remained within null expectations, and the direction-only test with fixed responders was weaker in both species (Supplementary Fig.~S12A,B). \textit{AP1S2} illustrates the pattern. It shifted strongly toward proximal PASs in both Xing2020 and Guan2022--0809 ($\Delta$DWUI $-0.531$ and $-0.475$), while its expression fell in one study and rose in the other ($\Delta$GEX $-1.22$ and $+3.53$; Supplementary Fig.~S12C,D).

Functional annotation identified only a few associations, each specific to one comparison. Relative to the expressed-gene background, matched tests associated mouse proximal P--S genes with ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis ($q=0.0422$). Relative to APA-testable genes, mouse proximal P--M genes were associated with integrated stress response signaling and with a KEGG lipid and atherosclerosis annotation ($q=0.0342$ each); the latter association reflects shared gene membership. None of these associations survived correction across each database's 28 analyses. The only association surviving this broader correction, human P--S intracellular protein transport ($q=0.0238$), describes APA-testable genes relative to all expressed genes and therefore reflects APA testability in general (Supplementary Fig.~S14A,B and Table~S24). Conditional power for modest associations was limited (Supplementary Fig.~S14D), so the functional organization of the recurrent genes remains open. We next asked whether genes that recurred within one species also responded in the other.

Excess cross-species sharing was supported only for selected stronger DWUI responses. Among jointly measurable one-to-one orthologs, only Xing2020 and Guo2019--CIP shared more same-direction P--S responses than expected after correction across the 24 primary tests, and only at the 0.05 threshold (130 observed against 105.31 expected, $q=0.0264$; Fig.~\ref{fig:cross-species-apa}A and Supplementary Fig.~S16A,B). Within the RWUI and MPRO summaries, the smallest $q$ values were 0.373 and 0.0808. This support also depended on the scope of correction. In a narrower eight-test DWUI family, three of four study pairs reached $q_8<0.05$ at 0.05 under at least one matching model, whereas a broader 56-test family that included directional components removed all corrected support (Fig.~\ref{fig:cross-species-apa}A and Supplementary Fig.~S16A,B).

Across the broader ortholog background, mean Spearman correlations between human and mouse effects were $-0.016$, $+0.015$ and $+0.020$ for R--S, E--S and P--S, each with an ortholog-block interval that included zero (Fig.~\ref{fig:cross-species-apa}B and Supplementary Fig.~S15A). Sharing appeared in particular sets and depended on the reference and on where genes started. Proximal responses defined against the co-captured M state were shared by 10 orthologs, against 3.46 and 3.88 expected under two matching models ($q=0.0038$ and 0.0045). Proximal responses defined against observed S were shared by 18 orthologs, close to the 13.91 and 14.43 expected ($q=0.1482$ and 0.1848; Fig.~\ref{fig:cross-species-apa}C and Supplementary Table~S17). Part of the S-referenced overlap reflected baseline PAS position. Matching for it raised the expected P--S overlap from 12.6 to 13.8, whereas the M-referenced overlap exceeded expectation at every added control (expected 2.7--3.5; Supplementary Fig.~S16D). Because the two sets were selected separately, their difference may reflect selection as well as the reference. This family of tests also differs in scope from the 24 primary tests and complements them.

Some genes nevertheless shifted proximally in both species despite opposite mean trends. Of the 18 shared P--S orthologs, 15 retained proximal support in systems with opposite documented-source mean shifts, nine also passed source and series checks, and eight remained proximal across four PAS, purity and coverage settings (Fig.~\ref{fig:cross-species-apa}D). \textit{SZRD1} is an example. It shifted proximally relative to M in both species ($-0.020$ and $-0.070$), but its shift relative to the source was $-0.049$ in Xing2020 and only $-0.016$ in Guo2019--CIP, below the 0.02 threshold (Fig.~\ref{fig:cross-species-apa}F). In these data, correspondence across species was therefore weaker than recurrence within species. Species coincides with source cells, protocol and the primed or naive character of the endpoint, any of which could contribute to this difference.
\subsection{PAS usage changes alter the retention of predicted miRNA and RBP sites in candidate intervals}

DWUI and MPRO each reduce a gene's PAS usage to a single value. To identify the sequence that transcripts gain or lose, we modeled the inclusion of transcript intervals within annotated terminal families. The inclusion $I$ of an interval is the fraction of a family's PAS usage that retains the complete interval, and $\Delta I$ compares P with S or M. Redistribution can add or remove an interval with little net shift, so the candidate pool combined both summaries. This DWUI--MPRO union contained 2,149 mouse and 2,343 human genes that either shifted in the same direction by $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.01$ in a fixed majority of eligible studies or met the MPRO 0.10 recurrence criterion (Supplementary Table~S17). It was defined separately from the recurrent sets of Figure~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}. P--S here is referenced to observed S cells, and P--M uses common qualified libraries.

Changed intervals tended to change in the same direction in both studies of a species, to an extent that depended on the contrast and on weighting. Across all evaluable region pairs, including those with opposite directions, mouse P--S direction agreement exceeded the marginal-sign reference by 11.0 percentage points (95\% gene-block interval 2.5--20.6; Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-regulatory-sites}A). In human P--S the region-weighted interval included zero, whereas weighting genes equally gave an excess of 18.9 points (4.8--31.6), compared with 11.6 points (3.4--19.9) in mouse P--S. In mouse P--M all 85 region pairs decreased in both studies, and the marginal reference was also 100\%, so the excess was zero and the marginal directions carried all of the agreement; human P--M contained only six pairs from two genes. The magnitudes of interval changes corresponded weakly between studies (Supplementary Fig.~S19D).

Redistribution also contributed candidates to the interval pool. Beyond the DWUI candidate pool, MPRO admitted 562 mouse and 1,127 human P--S candidates and 58 and 57 P--M candidates. Of the 208 mouse and 303 human P--S and 30 and 20 P--M additions evaluable in both studies, 17, 15, five and one carried shared strict inclusion changes (Supplementary Fig.~S19C).

These interval changes altered which predicted miRNA and RBP sites transcripts retained. A strict inclusion change required same-sign $|\Delta I|\geq10$ percentage points at both 20 and 50 UMIs. Shared intervals with such changes contained 3,576 miRNA-compatible sites in 76 mouse genes and 1,513 RBP-compatible sites in 68, and 519 and 525 sites in 30 and 28 human genes (Supplementary Table~S19). A broader set, all strictly changed intervals of each contrast, shared or study-specific, gave the net direction of retention in each gene when each site was weighted by the usage change of its interval. Human P--S genes on balance gained miRNA-compatible sites (19 of 29 genes with sites), whereas mouse P--S genes lost them (43 of 56), and all 30 mouse P--M genes lost them. RBP-compatible sites shifted in the same directions (17 of 27, 19 of 20 and 18 of 18 genes; Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-regulatory-sites}B and Supplementary Fig.~S19A). Like the inventory, it describes predicted site content.

Retention changed even though changed P--S intervals were not detectably richer in miRNA or RBP sites than equal-length stable windows in the same genes, matched for GC content and relative position ($q=0.902$--1; Supplementary Fig.~S20A,B and Table~S23). This comparison had little power: only 25 mouse and ten human genes could be matched, and a 10 sites/kb increase was detected in 8.7\% of human and 20.4\% of mouse simulations (Supplementary Fig.~S20C,D and Supplementary Fig.~S20E).

Expression data helped rank the candidate factors. Of the human factors with recurrent sites, 93 of 119 in P--S and 44 of 59 in P--M reached 2 CPM in a contributing endpoint library of both studies, and all six mouse direct-motif candidates were expressed in both mouse studies (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-regulatory-sites}C and Supplementary Fig.~S21B,C). Some factors with many predicted targets were barely expressed: \textit{ELAVL2}, the factor with the most recurrent target genes, remained below 2 CPM in every qualified Xing2020 state (Supplementary Table~S26). \textit{Rbm38}/\textit{RBM38} rose from S to P in all four studies, by 1.56--3.68 units of mean $\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$, yet its compatible sites were on balance less retained in the eight mouse target genes and more retained in the two human target genes, and human \textit{PCBP1} changed in opposite directions between the two human studies. These descriptive RNA-level contrasts provide expression context for ranking candidates, and direct tests are needed to show whether an RBP drives APA or whether APA alters its binding.

Within a gene, sites that changed inclusion often lay alongside constitutive sites. Within single studies and contrasts, 18.5\%--32.8\% of gene--factor relationships with at least two evaluable sites and one strict change contained both inclusion-variable and structurally constitutive sites, and 140 miRNA and 133 RBP relationships in mouse and 27 and 59 in human showed this exactly across studies (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-regulatory-sites}D). In \textit{Eif4ebp2}, one Pcbp1-compatible motif lay in a constitutive interval and two lay in inclusion-variable intervals of the same terminal family (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-regulatory-sites}E). Because of its broad state ranges, we use it to illustrate interval structure. Published long-read transcript models from reprogramming of mouse embryonic-stem-cell-derived neural progenitors (GSE282319) supported this structure\citep{Fort2026LongRead}. Isoforms sharing a complete splice chain differed in whether they retained the two variable \textit{Eif4ebp2} motifs, and likewise in whether they retained a miR-23-compatible site in \textit{Hmgn2} (Supplementary Fig.~S22E,F and Table~S27). A more proximal \textit{Eif4ebp2} isoform also excluded the motif modeled as constitutive, so constitutive refers to the PAS set we modeled. These public models come from a different reprogramming system and inform transcript structure only.

\textit{Rad23b} brings these observations together in one candidate. In both mouse studies, P reduced inclusion of the same 415-nt interval, which contains a miR-290/302-compatible seed match, by 11.48 and 19.37 percentage points relative to M, and the change passed the 50-UMI threshold (Fig.~\ref{fig:apa-regulatory-sites}F and Supplementary Figs.~S19C and S23A). The gene entered the interval analysis through redistribution: its net shift in Guo2019--CIP was small ($\Delta$DWUI $-0.0047$, compared with $-0.0422$ in Schiebinger2019--2i), whereas its study-native MPRO was 0.176 and 0.341, making it one of the five mouse P--M genes with shared strict inclusion changes among the 30 structurally evaluable MPRO additions. In the existing Schiebinger2019--2i well-level analysis, the gene-level P--M shift was also supported (MPRO $q=0.0341$, DWUI $q=0.0194$; Supplementary Results, ``Union inventory and MPRO additions'').

Public transcript models and an archived binding data set addressed the structure of this interval and its occupancy. In the long-read models, isoforms with the same splice chain ended on either side of the interval. A widely detected proximal isoform retained the first base of the interval but excluded the entire seed, and a rarer isoform excluded the whole interval. Archived AGO2 CLIP clusters from mouse embryonic stem cells (GSE25310)\citep{Leung2011Ago2} overlapped 145 bp of the interval in both wild-type and Dicer-knockout tracks, beginning 222 nt beyond the end of the seed, and the three wild-type library tracks filtered to remove Dicer-knockout clusters lay outside the interval (Supplementary Fig.~S23C and Table~S28). The archive therefore leaves seed-level, miRNA-dependent binding unresolved. Because the interval and its seed were selected descriptively, their function remains a hypothesis for testing.

Across seven reprogramming studies, mean PAS position moved in different directions in different systems, yet within each species the same genes shifted in the same direction in independent studies more often than expected. In these systems, global shortening or lengthening is therefore an incomplete description of APA during reprogramming, and the reproducible signal lies in which genes shift: recurrence exceeded conditional expectation at the gene level, although individual memberships were sensitive to measurement choices. The distal trend in Xing2020 contrasts with the $3'$ UTR shortening reported in bulk analyses of somatic cell reprogramming\citep{JiTian2009}. Part of this contrast reflects what is measured: DWUI describes relative position on a study-specific PAS axis, whereas the bulk analyses measured UTR length, and the studies differ in source cells, protocols and sampled states. The opposition persisted in nucleotide units within tandem $3'$ UTRs, so it extends beyond the index. The same bulk analyses found higher-than-random agreement among data sets\citep{JiTian2009}. The present data define how far such agreement extends at single-cell resolution, for explicit state comparisons and between species.

Endpoint comparisons capture only part of the remodeling. One class of genes shifted distally at intermediate states and returned toward the source configuration by P, consistent with the non-monotonic PAS dynamics resolved by SCAPE in a mouse time course\citep{Zhou2022SCAPE}. Cross-study comparisons built on endpoint contrasts, including ours, will therefore undercount genes whose PAS usage changes during reprogramming. The class frequencies refer to genes selected for cross-study similarity. The prevalence of each form, and whether it differs between species, require separately sampled cohorts.

What a recurrent gene represents depends on the reference state, on the summary of PAS usage and on the expression context. Of 200 measurable mouse P--M recurrent genes, 97 also met the same criterion against the somatic source in both studies (78 of 146 human genes in Xing2020 alone), and in both mouse studies \textit{Slc38a2} was more proximal in P than in either S or M, although M differed from S in opposite directions. Net-position and redistribution summaries recovered partly different genes from the same measurements. \textit{Nudt21}, a cleavage factor whose depletion enhances reprogramming\citep{Brumbaugh2018}, was strongly redistributed between P and S in one mouse study with little net shift in either. Conversely, \textit{CDKN1A}, which encodes the p53 target p21 that restricts reprogramming\citep{Hong2009p21}, shifted net position recurrently relative to M while its MPRO stayed below 0.10 in both supporting studies (Supplementary Table~S21A). Recurrence also occurred in genes whose expression changed in opposite directions between studies, most clearly in human, consistent with the partly distinct gene sets reported in larger single-cell analyses\citep{Fansler2024}. Because the direction-only test with fixed responders was weaker (Supplementary Fig.~S12A,B), this result shows that APA adds information in these expression contexts, while its general relation to expression remains open. Functional associations were local, each confined to particular comparisons, within the limited power of these tests.

Recurrence within species extended only weakly across species. Corrected support was confined to selected stronger DWUI comparisons, and continuous effects barely corresponded across orthologs. Part of the overlap in the S-referenced set reflected where genes start on their PAS axes, whereas the M-referenced overlap remained above expectation under every control, although the two sets came from different candidate pools. Species also coincides with protocol, source cells and endpoint identity. Human iPSC and mouse 2i endpoints differ along the primed--naive axis, and M combines heterogeneous mesenchymal and extracellular-matrix-retaining populations. Comparative cleavage-site atlases align homologous positions across species\citep{Derti2012,Wang2018Conserved}, whereas our PAS axes represent relative position within each study. Whether individual sites are regulated in a conserved manner therefore remains open.

At the sequence level, PAS usage changes altered which predicted miRNA and RBP sites transcripts retained. Single-cell APA atlases have reported predicted-site content in the same descriptive way, by intersecting predicted miRNA sites with APA-variable regions or by weighting site counts by isoform usage\citep{Lee2022FlyAPA,Yang2022scAPAatlas}. Retention reflects changes in interval usage, whereas density measures the concentration of predicted sites within an interval. PAS shifts can therefore alter site retention without density enrichment. Changing and constitutive sites for the same factor often coexisted in one terminal family, so a shift can alter the number of sites while other compatible sites remain in the modeled transcripts. Public long-read models from a study of isoform switching during reprogramming\citep{Fort2026LongRead} contained, at three loci, isoforms with the same splice chain that retained or excluded the modeled sites, and they also showed that a site is constitutive only relative to the PASs modeled. As in the mouse embryo atlas, which used RBP expression to nominate candidate regulators\citep{Agarwal2021}, most candidate RBPs with recurrent sites were expressed at the compared endpoints of both human studies, whereas some factors with many predicted targets, such as \textit{ELAVL2}, were barely expressed in one. \textit{Rbm38} rose from S to P in all four studies while its compatible sites changed retention in different directions between species. Expression and sequence compatibility can therefore prioritize candidates, whereas the sign of regulation requires direct measurement. Sequence compatibility, RNA expression, measured occupancy, protein output and reprogramming phenotype are separate levels of evidence, and this study addresses the first two.

\textit{Rad23b} offers a concrete hypothesis that links predicted-site retention to protein output and reprogramming. In both mouse studies, P reduced inclusion of an interval containing a seed match shared by miR-290 and miR-302 family members. Of these, miR-291-3p, miR-294 and miR-295 increase the efficiency of reprogramming by Oct4, Sox2 and Klf4, an effect lost when cMyc is added\citep{Judson2009ESCC}. RAD23B participates in an OCT4/SOX2 coactivator complex implicated in reprogramming\citep{Fong2011SCC}. If the seed is functional, isoforms that end before it should respond less to these miRNAs, which could change RAD23B output as cells acquire pluripotency. The long-read models support the structural premise, because the proximal isoform excludes the complete seed. Three links remain untested. The AGO2 archive is uninformative about seed-specific, miRNA-dependent binding\citep{Leung2011Ago2}, and the activity of the seed and its consequences for protein and reprogramming remain to be measured. The interval was also selected descriptively, although the gene-level P--M shift had well-level support. Reporters carrying the $3'$ UTR with an intact or mutated seed, in cells with different miR-290/302 activity, together with endogenous PAS perturbation and measurements of RAD23B protein and reprogramming efficiency, would test the prediction. Such tests matter because $3'$ UTR isoform choice had limited effects on stability, translation or protein abundance in mouse fibroblasts and proliferating T cells\citep{Spies2013,Gruber2014}.

Several features of the design bound these conclusions. Documented-source contrasts were available in only two studies per species, each with limited source replication, and source and P states also differed in collection date and medium. Independent-well replication came from one mouse cell line, and external PAS-seq covered only part of the candidates. The S, P and M labels align broad categories across studies, and populations with matching expression signatures may still differ between studies. The controls were defined after the original analysis. They retained the aggregate excess and part of the individual memberships, so single genes should be treated as candidates, and systematic differences between states could remain. The interval analysis began from a separately selected candidate pool, an upstream dependence outside the scope of the marginal-direction reference, and it forms an analysis separate from the gene-level tests in Figure~\ref{fig:apa-recurrence-context}. Finally, the interval model assigns reads to annotated PAS coordinates, and binding, stability and protein output require measurements beyond motif compatibility.

\subsection{PAS identification, filtering and annotation}

Strand-aware coverage valleys and coverage decreases identified candidate PAS intervals, which were filtered for overlap with internal-priming masks and proximity to same-strand splice-donor sites. Both filters acted on candidate intervals before PAS selection and quantification. PAS--barcode--UMI observations were deduplicated, merged within studies and annotated. Primary sites required same-strand terminal assignment, whereas the reference-supported layer additionally required an external coordinate within 50 nt from PolyA\_DB v4.1, PolyASite v3.0, GENCODE release 44 for human or M33 for mouse\citep{Yu2026PolyADB4,Moon2025PolyASite,Frankish2023GENCODE,GENCODEHuman44,GENCODEMouseM33}. Expanded-primary sensitivity excluded relaxed sites. Detection, projected zeros and coordinate-proxy rules are detailed in Supplementary Methods.
\subsection{APA quantification and state comparisons}

Genes required two supported PASs on one chromosome/strand. Position weights $r_i$ scale the complete study-primary catalog from proximal 0 to distal 1 before layer selection. SEACells metacells used up to 30 principal components, a 15-neighbor kernel, 10--100 iterations, a target of approximately 50 cells per metacell and seed 20260905\citep{Persad2023SEACells}. For each metacell, \[ \mathrm{DWUI}_{gm}=\frac{\sum_i c_{mi}r_{gi}}{\sum_i c_{mi}}. \] Here $c_{mi}$ is PAS count. Primary criteria required at least 20 gene-level PAS UMIs, state purity at least 0.8, and at least three metacells/30 cells per library--state. Endpoint estimates additionally required gene-qualified metacells to contain 30 cells, with comparison-specific support rules provided in Supplementary Methods. Qualifying metacells were averaged within library--state groups. Negative/positive target-minus-reference effects indicate proximal/distal shifts in relative PAS position. Physical transcript length lies outside this measure.
\subsection{APA dynamics and expression changes}

Profile candidates required paired-study coverage, DWUI range at least 0.01 and matched-state correlation at least 0.6. Species-balanced $k$-means classified centered, unit-norm profiles at $k=3$, a parsimonious working resolution after comparing $k=2$--6 by silhouette width, inertia and species-specific cluster size (Supplementary Methods). Complete profiles used \[ L=|R-S|+|E-R|+|P-E|,\qquad D=|P-S|,\qquad T=1-D/L. \] DWUI--GEX comparisons used identical states and $\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$ expression, with CPM denoting counts per million. Moran's $I$ assessed within-study expression-graph organization, adjusting state/coverage and permuting within library--state blocks. Details and sensitivities are in Supplementary Methods.

Recurrence required same-direction support from at least two studies at $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.02$ (primary) or 0.05. Within each study, all evaluable series had to agree, and each study contributed once. Nulls used 10,000 stratified permutations preserving observability, event frequencies, expression, APA coverage, PAS number, reference DWUI and directional capacity. Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) adjustment covered eight species--contrast--threshold tests.

Six-rule P--S consensus used a fixed catalog, fixed-gene or common-contributor backgrounds, joint event-vector permutations and four-test families per view. Dual-reference analyses descriptively traced the original P--M candidates through matched P/M/S measurements. APA/GEX response-identity nulls matched expression response and APA covariates, whereas direction-only nulls additionally fixed responder status. GEX directions required concordant series and $|\Delta\mathrm{GEX}|\geq0.25$. The larger one-sided $P$ across shuffle orientations entered eight-test correction. Coverage, aggregation, permutation and example-selection rules are given in Supplementary Methods.

Ensembl release 116 high-confidence one-to-one orthologs were retrieved through BioMart on 1 August 2026\citep{Dyer2025Ensembl,Kinsella2011BioMart}. Documented-source concordance used four study pairs, 10,000 independent signed-label permutations and thresholds of 0.02/0.05. The primary reporting family covered 24 tests spanning DWUI, RWUI and MPRO. Figure~4A additionally displays an exploratory eight-test family for same-direction DWUI sharing and marks the single result retained by the primary family; an exploratory 24-test within-DWUI family that also includes proximal and distal components is reported in Supplementary Table~S16. A 56-test family including all signed components served as the broadest sensitivity analysis. Matching preserved expression, APA coverage, PAS number, observability and source DWUI under source-DWUI-quintile (Q5) or series-range (R10) matching.

Separate observed-S P--S/paired P--M proximal sets at 0.02 required proximal support in both mouse and at least two human studies, with any opposite human effects kept below the strong-effect threshold. Their 20,000-permutation nulls matched node-reference covariates and PAS support, retaining the 16,092-ortholog universe with unmeasurable members in their corresponding strata. Continuous effects and cis-feature Firth models used separate matched/conditional tests. Cis features were added to discovery-effect, testability, PAS-count and recurrence covariates, and joint tests used 4,999 conditional bootstrap draws. Full backgrounds, 32-configuration cis correction and training-fold preprocessing for repeated five-fold cross-validation are in Supplementary Methods. Study-specific PAS axes represent relative within-study positions, while homologous cleavage-site alignment requires a separate framework.
\subsection{Candidate miRNA and RBP recognition-interval inclusion analysis}

Candidates combined a DWUI candidate pool requiring same-direction effects of at least 0.01 in a fixed majority of eligible studies with MPRO 0.10 recurrent genes. Canonical miRNA seeds and provenance-labeled RBP motifs were scanned on the annotated UTR strand with FIMO v5.5.2 at a per-hit threshold of $10^{-4}$\citep{Kozomara2019miRBase,Fromm2020MirGeneDB,Grant2011FIMO}. Inclusion was \[ I_{is\ell}=\frac{\sum_j n_{js\ell}R_{ij}}{\sum_j n_{js\ell}}, \] where $n$ is annotated-PAS count and $R$ indicates complete interval retention. Libraries required terminal-family coverage of at least 0.5. Strict changes required same-sign $|\Delta I|\geq10$ pp at 20/50 UMIs with at least five included and five excluded support UMIs per state at the 50-UMI cutoff. P--S used observed-S separate-state means, whereas P--M inventories and tests used common-library paired means. The descriptive \textit{Eif4ebp2} profile retained separate-state library-equal means. Canonical seed matches and motif scans indicate sequence compatibility, while experimental binding remains to be tested.

External checks used the published filtered long-read transcript models, abundance table and support annotations from GSE282319\citep{Fort2026LongRead}, and the doRiNA archive of GSE25310 AGO2 clusters\citep{Leung2011Ago2}. We fixed the existing \textit{Rad23b}, \textit{Hmgn2} and \textit{Eif4ebp2} intervals before examining those resources. Long-read models were compared for complete splice-chain identity and terminal inclusion/exclusion. The existing \textit{Rad23b} interval and seed were tested for same-strand overlap with the archived WT and Dicer-knockout clusters after reciprocal coordinate conversion. These were structure and archive-coordinate checks, without raw-read reanalysis or state-differential usage/binding tests; full procedures and provenance are in Supplementary Methods, Supplementary Figs.~S22E,F and S23B,C and Tables~S27--S28.

Supplementary Methods document partition, state-member, PAS-layer, counting and coverage sensitivities. Follow-up controls added within-library measurement bootstrap intervals, same-state halves, equal gene-PAS depths, cycle-score matching, complete common-axis inventories and exact series-identity-matched nulls (Supplementary Fig.~S9A,C; Table~S22). A full-background no-reversal simulation repeated trajectory selection and clustering (Supplementary Fig.~S7G,H). These analyses were specified after inspecting the original results, condition on the observed design and retain coverage failures separately from zero effects. Public GSE99922 PAS-seq supplied an exploratory external usage comparison with fixed candidate rosters (Table~S23). \Reserved{Alternative PAS callers (SCAPE-APA, polyApipe) were run on the same reads and frozen cells; versions, scope and matching rules are in Supplementary Methods (Supplementary Fig.~S5)}.

Primary reporting used documented-source P--S and paired P--M DWUI at 0.02, with 0.05 as a stronger-response sensitivity in the same complete eight-test species--contrast--threshold family. RWUI/MPRO, counting-rule consensus, selected profile classes, cross-species comparisons and interval models addressed secondary questions with their own stated inventories (Supplementary Table~S17). Cross-species study-pair reporting used the complete 24-test cross-metric family; narrower families remained exploratory. The new measurement/background analyses were defined after inspection of the original results and did not constitute preregistration or replace the original families.

Permutation tests used fixed seeds and one-count corrections, with BH families stated per analysis. Biological replication was assessed at the study or independent-well level; cells, metacells and sites served as measurement units. With a fixed PAS catalog and identical contributor weights, $\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}=\sum_i r_i\Delta p_i$ and $\mathrm{MPRO}=\max_i\Delta p_i-\min_i\Delta p_i$. MPRO was computed after aggregating proportion vectors, thereby preserving signed library contributions before the unsigned range. The five-metric comparison included DWUI, RWUI, MPRO and distal/proximal supported-catalog endpoint proportions (PDUI/PPUI). Metric-specific nulls matched references and change capacity.

Schiebinger2019 P--M eligibility required at least four dates with at least two independent qualified wells per date. Dates received equal weight, and wells were averaged within dates. Synchronized vector sign flips tested zero-centered symmetric well differences, recomputing MPRO after aggregation, with joint BH across $5\times268$ tests. All wells came from one cell line, so inference addressed independent wells within that line. P--S endpoint tests counted the two-source variance once, while state/date/medium confounding restricted interpretation. Panariello2023 inference used independent pools after collapsing technical captures.

Separate secondary tests addressed composition and pathway context. Fisher tests assessed conditional integer-count composition at the count level. Biological-replicate differential APA requires a separate design. GO/KEGG tests used hypergeometric and covariate-matched comparisons\citep{Ashburner2000GO,GeneOntology2026,Kanehisa2025KEGG}. Exact formulas, simulation error, coverage exclusions and route-specific software records are in Supplementary Methods and the reproducibility archive.

In the reprogramming systems examined, mean PAS shifts differed in direction, yet within each species individual genes shifted PAS usage in the same direction across independent studies more often than expected, and this recurrence extended only weakly to the other species. At the transcript level, PAS usage changes altered the retention of predicted miRNA and RBP sites in candidate intervals. These intervals provide testable candidates for how PAS choice contributes to pluripotency acquisition.

\subsection{PAS catalog, DWUI and state comparisons}
\subsubsection{PAS identification and catalog}

Candidate PASs were called independently in each library from strand-aware genomic BAM coverage. Read length was the modal length of the first 10,000 alignments; alignment blocks were accumulated by transcript-oriented strand and smoothed with a triangular kernel of half-width half the read length. Valleys in the smoothed profile and the maximum coverage decrease between adjacent intervals (minimum 20) defined candidate regions. The fixed coordinate was the downstream valley boundary shifted upstream in transcript orientation by $\lfloor L/2\rfloor$ nt, where $L$ is the read length; this coordinate is a cleavage-site proxy at coverage resolution.

Two filters acted on the full half-open candidate intervals before PAS selection and quantification. Internal-priming masks were generated by scanning unspliced annotated gene spans for forward-strand A-rich and reverse-strand T-rich stretches (at least 10 nt, at most one mismatch). The strand-oriented start of each stretch defined a genomic interval extending 500 bp upstream and 20 bp downstream, with upstream extension clipped at the corresponding gene-span boundary. Overlapping mask intervals were merged by chromosome and strand, and candidates overlapping a same-strand mask were excluded. Chromosome names were normalized to the same \texttt{chr} namespace for overlap queries.

Splice-donor evidence was collected from CIGAR introns of 70--500,000 nt. An intron was retained with at least 20 supporting alignments and a maximum anchor length of at least 8 nt on each side across those alignments. For the zero-based intron interval $[a,b)$, the donor point was $a-1$ on the positive strand or $b$ on the negative strand. A candidate interval $[s,e)$ was excluded if a same-strand donor point lay in $[s-10,e+100)$ on the positive strand or $[s-100,e+10)$ on the negative strand. These windows were applied to candidate intervals, independently of the fixed PAS coordinate; acceptor sites were not separately masked.

Quantification retained mapped, non-duplicate primary alignments from accepted barcodes carrying \texttt{CB} and \texttt{UB} tags. The read endpoint (\texttt{reference\_end}$-1$ on the positive strand, \texttt{reference\_start} on the negative strand) was assigned to half-open candidate intervals on the transcript strand, to the most downstream interval when one block overlapped several, and each PAS--barcode--UMI combination counted once. Within each study, sites on the same chromosome and strand separated by at most 25 bp were merged, with clusters limited to 50 bp. Sites detected in at least two libraries formed the core catalog and single-library sites were retained as private evidence. Annotation against gene models distinguished same-strand $3'$ UTR or terminal-exon assignments, transcript-end rescue, and antisense, multi-gene or unassigned sites, defining primary, relaxed and excluded tiers; analyses used the primary tier, and relaxed sites entered only designated sensitivity outputs. Study-level matrices summed library-specific counts mapped to the merged catalog, so a catalog site absent from a library's calls received a projected zero labeled separately from observed zero usage.
\subsubsection{DWUI and coverage rules}

APA analyses included genes with at least two primary PASs on one chromosome and strand. Sites were ordered in the direction of transcription, and the relative position of site $j$ in gene $g$ was \[ r_{gj}=\frac{x_{gj}-\min_{k} x_{gk}}{\max_{k} x_{gk}-\min_{k} x_{gk}}, \] with $x$ the strand-oriented coordinate and extrema taken over the complete primary catalog of the gene in that study. The primary layer required each site to have an external cleavage coordinate within 50 nt; the \texttt{expanded\_primary} sensitivity included all primary sites. Both layers kept the complete-catalog weights, so the axis extremes may fall outside the supported subset.

Metacells were built within each library with SEACells\citep{Persad2023SEACells} from normalized highly variable gene expression (10,000 counts per cell, log-transformed, up to 30 principal components, 15-neighbor kernel, 10--100 iterations), targeting about 50 cells per metacell (seed 20260905) and independently of time or state labels. Metacell PAS and expression counts summed member cells. For gene $g$ and metacell $m$, with $c_{mi}$ the count at selected site $i$, \[ a_{gm}=\frac{\sum_{i\in g} c_{mi}\,r_{gi}}{\sum_{i\in g} c_{mi}} \] defined the distance-weighted PAS usage index (DWUI). Values from fewer than 20 PAS UMIs were missing, and zero-count sites kept their weights.

A library--state group required at least three metacells and 30 cells, and a gene at least three metacells meeting the 20-UMI threshold. The Figure~1D overview and Figure~2 applied the 30-cell rule to the whole group; the endpoint estimates of Figure~1D (lower) and Figure~3 required the gene-qualified metacells themselves to contain 30 cells. Within a route, a site was supported when it had at least 10 UMIs in at least two metacells, and a gene was eligible with two supported sites. Metacells needed state purity (fraction of members in the majority state) of at least 0.8. Gene-level DWUI was averaged over qualifying metacells within library--state groups, and $\Delta$DWUI was the target-minus-reference difference. Library-balanced state means weighted libraries equally. All contrasts used study-specific PAS measurements (Table~\ref{tab:analysis-definitions}).

Three reference designs were kept distinct. The observed-S overview (Figure~1D, upper) used, within each analysis group, the common evaluable genes across S and every observed R, E, P or M state, and averaged library-balanced DWUI(state)$-$DWUI(S) with equal gene weight and all effect sizes included; its S could include induced or mixed samples. The documented-source P--S contrast used D0, source or Stage I day 0 libraries. A gene needed estimable library--state means at both ends and at least two PASs, each supported by ten pooled UMIs in two metacells across the paired groups. Pairwise effects were averaged across library pairs within source--target sampling-unit pairs, then across source units within dates and across dates, and then across target units and dates. This estimator served both the global summaries (Figure~1D, lower; Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}A--E) and within-species recurrence. Global summaries weighted genes equally in means, medians and fractions beyond $\pm\tau$ ($\tau=0.02$, 0.05), with subthreshold genes in the denominator. The two Guan2022 series were displayed separately but formed one study; Liu2020, lacking a separable documented source, and Panariello2023, with an induced D3 reference, were excluded from documented-source analyses. Paired P--M compared states within the same physical library.

Four measurement settings were compared: reference-supported PASs with purity $\geq0.8$ (primary), purity $\geq0.9$, at least five qualifying metacells at each end, and expanded primary PASs with purity $\geq0.8$. Each was summarized on its available genes, the within-route intersection across settings, the within-species intersection (2,051 human and 1,667 mouse genes) and 710 orthologs measurable in all five series and settings; ranges across these are descriptive minima and maxima. Source sensitivity used each documented source separately for Guan2022--0618 and Schiebinger2019--2i, on available genes, a fixed gene intersection and target-library pairs evaluable against every source.

For the tandem-$3'$ UTR subset, all retained primary PASs of a gene had to lie within the $3'$ UTR of one stop-codon-containing terminal exon of at least one coding transcript in assembly-matched Ensembl release 116\citep{Dyer2025Ensembl}, with exact coordinates. Multiplying $\Delta$DWUI by the strand-oriented PAS span gave a position difference in nucleotides. Available genes, fixed within-route and within-species intersections and the all-route cross-species intersection were evaluated separately. These are annotation-compatible position changes.

PAS quantification was checked by BAM recounting, split-half comparisons, UMI thinning (fractions 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0, 20 repeats; 1.0 as an identity check), sequence context and locus inspection. Coverage sensitivity raised the per-metacell threshold from 20 to 40 or 80 PAS UMIs in the fixed 540-mouse and 897-human trajectory cohorts, keeping the gene--route--contrast denominator and marking contrasts that became unevaluable.

A fixed-catalog recount tested documented-source P--S recurrence under six counting rules across all 38 source/endpoint libraries of Xing2020, Guan2022 (both series), Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i, with state assignments, metacells, target PASs and complete-catalog weights fixed. The rules were original library-specific intervals with sample-PAS--cell--UMI deduplication; the same intervals with atlas-PAS--cell--UMI deduplication; transferred atlas windows restricted to called PASs; unrestricted transferred windows; and windows clipped against all primary PASs or against the full atlas. Transferred windows placed the study-wide median left/right sample-to-atlas widths around the atlas representative, clipping used same-strand adjacent-coordinate midpoints, and an endpoint could contribute to every overlapping window with atlas-PAS--cell--UMI deduplication. A gene with an invalid window was unavailable under that rule. The fixed-gene view kept genes measurable under all six rules; the common-contributor view also fixed metacells and endpoint library pairs qualifying under every rule. Study-level labels were rebuilt with the all-evaluable-series rule at 0.02 and 0.05, and the unrestricted estimator recovered every label.

Each view--rule combination had recurrence permutations preserving measurability, expression, APA coverage, PAS number, reference DWUI and directional capacity, with four species--threshold tests per BH family. Counting-rule consensus required same-direction support from at least two studies under all six rules. Its null shuffled each study--gene's six-rule event vector as a block within the intersection of the six matching strata, fixing rule-specific counts and cross-rule dependence; each of the eight tests used 10,000 permutations with four-test BH within each view. The minimum fraction of gene vectors in nonsingleton strata was 0.689. Paired P--M was outside the recount.
\subsubsection{Comparison with alternative PAS callers}

\subsection{State-resolved DWUI profiles}

Profiles were referenced to S within each route, and gene expression was quantified in the same APA-eligible metacells as $\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$. Candidates came from three study pairs: Schiebinger2019--2i with Guo2019--CIP on S--R--E--P, Xing2020 with Guan2022--0618 on S--R--P, and Xing2020 with Liu2020 on S--E--P. A gene had to meet the PAS and metacell criteria in both studies, have all paired states observed, a DWUI range of at least 0.01 in each study and a Pearson correlation of at least 0.6 between matched-state profiles; the correlation served as a selection criterion. The mouse pair gave 540 genes. The two human pairs gave 651 and 343 (96 shared), and their union was further required to have a complete Xing2020 S--R--E--P profile with range at least 0.01, leaving 897.

Class-specific APA scores centered each gene's DWUI across evaluable metacells within a study and averaged centered values with equal gene weight within each class; scores were projected onto member cells only for display. Local organization was tested on symmetric binary $k$-nearest-neighbor graphs built from a 30-dimensional expression latent space within each study ($k=20$ primary), using within-study expression edges only and metacell purity $\geq0.8$. Baseline Moran's $I$ was compared with 9,999 within-study permutations. The conditional analysis regressed each score on coarse state, $\log(1+\text{number of DWUI-estimable genes})$ and $\log(1+\text{PAS UMIs})$ and permuted residuals within library--state blocks. One-sided permutation $P$ values were $(1+n_{\mathrm{exceed}})/10{,}000$. Baseline and state-only analyses formed a 42-test BH family (state-only results in the source data) and the state- and coverage-adjusted analyses a 21-test family. Sensitivities rebuilt the $k=20$ graphs on fixed gene panels requiring DWUI in at least 70\%, 80\% or 90\% of eligible metacells per study and class (combinations with fewer than 30 complete-case metacells omitted) and repeated the conditional model at $k=10$, 15, 20 and 30, each with its own BH family.
\subsubsection{APA--expression correspondence}

Correspondence used gene--route profiles with S and at least two further jointly measured states and nonconstant profiles. Pearson and Spearman correlations between observed-S-referenced $\Delta$DWUI and $\Delta\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$ on identical states were descriptive. For adjacent transitions, a pair was same-direction only when both changes had the same nonzero sign; zero changes stayed in the denominator.

Recurrence was evaluated separately by species for documented-source P--S and paired P--M, on the reference-supported primary layer with purity $\geq0.8$. Directional evidence required $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.02$, with 0.05 as the stronger threshold. A study contributed one directional vote only when all its evaluable routes or series had the same sign and reached the threshold; multiple series in one GEO study counted as one study. A recurrent gene had same-direction support from at least two studies, allowing an opposing study. Reference DWUI was reconstructed from the qualified comparisons and their sampling-unit and date weights (S for P--S, co-captured M for P--M), with the median across series representing a multi-series study. For each species, contrast and threshold, 10,000 permutations preserved every study's measurable genes and its numbers of positive, negative and non-event genes within strata of expression, APA coverage, PAS number, eligible-study count, reference-DWUI quintile and the capacity of every eligible series to accommodate a shift of the tested size in each direction. The statistic was the number of recurrent genes, with upper-tail $P$ values and BH over the eight species--contrast--threshold tests. Human P--M support was also tabulated as exactly one, two or three studies. Leave-one-study-out analyses rebuilt strata and null after each deletion, and treating the two Guan2022 series separately was a sensitivity analysis.
\subsubsection{Alternative PAS-usage summaries}

The multi-metric analysis kept the supported catalog, purity and coverage rules and qualified library pairs. Within each eligible metacell, counts were normalized to PAS proportions (zero-count sites included), averaged equally across metacells within library--state groups and aggregated with the sampling-unit/date hierarchy. For $n$ supported PASs ordered by transcription, the rank-weighted usage index was $\mathrm{RWUI}=\sum_i p_i i/n$, and the endpoint indices were $\mathrm{PDUI}=p_n$ and $\mathrm{PPUI}=p_1$. PDUI and PPUI are defined analogously to the distal-usage index of DaPars\citep{Xia2014DaPars} and the proximal-usage index of scAPA\citep{Shulman2019}, here as the endpoint proportions of the supported catalog, which need not coincide with the complete-catalog endpoints that define DWUI weights. For the aggregated difference $d_i=p_{i,\mathrm{target}}-p_{i,\mathrm{reference}}$, maximum proportion redistribution was $\mathrm{MPRO}=\max_i d_i-\min_i d_i$ (range 0--2, unsigned), computed after vector aggregation. Two-PAS indices can be affine rescalings, so genes with at least three supported PASs were summarized separately; when two PASs occupy the axis endpoints, $\Delta\mathrm{RWUI}=0.5\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}$ and $\mathrm{MPRO}=2|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|$.

DWUI and RWUI used thresholds of 0.02/0.05 and MPRO 0.10/0.20. Signed events and recurrence followed the DWUI rules; an MPRO event required all measurable series to exceed the unsigned threshold, and MPRO recurrence meant at least two responding studies with any PAS change. Metric-specific nulls preserved study measurability, within-stratum label counts and the study-level expression, APA coverage and joint-PAS covariates. Signed metrics also matched their reference quintile and directional capacity; MPRO matched reference concentration $\sum_i p_i^2$, maximum possible redistribution $1-\min_i p_i+\max_i p_i$ and threshold eligibility. Labels were shuffled within each study, with 10,000 permutations (seed 20260930) and upper-tail $P=(1+\#\{T_{\mathrm{null}}\geq T_{\mathrm{observed}}\})/10{,}001$. BH families were the eight recurrence tests per metric and all 24 tests. These strata ignored the number and identity combination of measurable series within a study, so heterogeneous series configurations could still influence the reported values.

\emph{Conditional intervals.} For each gene, 500 bootstrap samples drew qualified metacells with replacement within each library--state and averaged their PAS proportions; the source/target date and unit weights then aggregated proportion vectors before DWUI and MPRO were computed. A source library received one resampled vector per draw, shared by all comparisons reusing it. Percentile 95\% intervals quantify within-library measurement variation. The interval-supported DWUI setting required every measurable series' interval to exclude zero in the called direction; for MPRO, the observed range had to exceed the 95th percentile of the centered bootstrap-error range.

\emph{Same-state halves.} Each qualified library--state's metacells were split into two balanced halves 100 times. Each half needed three qualified metacells and 30 cells, and the pair needed two PASs with ten UMIs in two metacells. S/S and P/P differences kept the endpoint weighting and reused the same source split across targets; study votes required the complete set of measurable series. Recurrence was recalculated on each pseudo-comparison's exact background. Halves estimate measurement and within-state heterogeneity at reduced depth, whereas systematic bias between distinct states requires other controls. A calibrated diagnostic used half the sum of target and reference half differences as an approximate full-depth error model.

\emph{Depth, cycle and common axis.} PAS counts were subsampled without replacement to exactly 20 or 40 UMIs per gene and metacell (20 draws each), metacells below depth were unavailable, and qualification and weights were reapplied; the first draw, fixed in advance, entered the permutation test and all draws supplied stability summaries. These are equal gene-PAS depths, and Spearman correlations between signed effects and differences in $\log_2$ mean gene-PAS depth were descriptive. Cycle matching split S-phase and G2/M program scores into route-specific tertiles (up to nine joint bins), kept bins present in both states of a library pair with weights proportional to the smaller metacell count, and required three metacells and 30 cells per side; it balances expression-based scores of cycle phase. The common axis paired Guo2019--CIP with Schiebinger2019--2i and Xing2020 with Guan2022: reference-supported PASs on a common chromosome and strand were clustered within 50 nt, clusters present in both studies (at least two per gene) were placed on a strand-oriented 0--1 axis of cluster-mean positions, and member counts were summed before eligibility was reapplied. Human P--M had a single eligible study on this axis.

\emph{Series-identity matching and correction.} Each setting used 10,000 permutations preserving gene covariates, event frequencies, directional or redistribution capacity and eligible-study count, with an added stratum for the exact measurable series combination (including Guan2022--0618 versus --0809). DWUI 0.02/0.05 and MPRO 0.10/0.20 each kept their eight positions; unavailable positions entered BH as $P=1$. The native null, both series-matched and unmatched, the interval-supported, two depth, cycle and common-axis settings formed one 112-position family, including 12 unavailable positions.

\emph{Nested backgrounds and signal injection.} Within-species DWUI recurrence was recomputed under a ladder that first fixed exact study/series identities, eligible-study count, directional feasibility and study-level event margins and then added expression/APA coverage, baseline position and PAS number, with a PAS-first path as an alternative; all eight positions used 10,000 draws per model. Signal injection drew two normally distributed gene preferences shared across studies, one per direction, with log-weight standard deviations 0, 0.5, 1 and 2; within complete strata, weighted sampling without replacement assigned the fixed negative count and then the fixed positive count. Each strength had 1,000 replicates. These simulations measure the power of the fixed-event recurrence statistic alone.

Dual-reference tracing followed the 0.02 P--M recurrent cohorts with membership and direction fixed. Complete comparisons required qualified P and M from the same physical target library and collection time and the same documented-source S library for P--S and M--S; Xing2020, Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i supplied complete triplets. Each contrast needed two jointly supported PASs, each with ten pooled UMIs in two qualified metacells, and P, M and S used identical contributors and the documented-source hierarchy, checked against $\mathrm{P{-}S}=\mathrm{P{-}M}+\mathrm{M{-}S}$. Membership required P--S and P--M to keep the P--M sign and reach 0.02 in both mouse studies, or within Xing2020 for human; denominators separated original members, complete measurements and members retaining the P--M response, and missing values were kept separate from subthreshold values. Sensitivities used a 0.05 effect threshold on the same cohort, purity 0.9, the expanded primary layer, and at least five qualified metacells in each of P, M and S.

Matched MPRO recovered PAS-proportion vectors from integer counts on the same axes, averaged them over the same qualified metacells and aggregated P, M and S over the identical triplets and weights. MPRO was the range of the aggregated target-minus-reference vector, reproducing the matched DWUI effects and the vector identity above with MPRO computed after aggregation (threshold 0.10; five-metacell coverage sensitivity). The source-connected follow-up (Table~\ref{tab:matched-state-metrics}) applied this aggregation to the P--M DWUI-only, shared and MPRO-only recurrent memberships at $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.02$ and MPRO $\geq0.10$, in Guo2019--CIP, Schiebinger2019--2i and Xing2020. Recurrence-defined additions compared MPRO 0.10/0.20 with DWUI 0.02/0.05 membership; significance-defined additions required MPRO $q<0.05$ and DWUI $q\geq0.05$ within the 1,340-test well family below.

\emph{Schiebinger2019 wells.} Destructive-sampling culture wells\citep{Schiebinger2019} from one cell line supplied repeated measurements; batch labels marked collection groups only. P--M retained genes with qualified states in each well and at least four collection dates with two qualified wells, weighting dates equally and wells equally within dates. Each well supplied a paired PAS-proportion difference vector, a count-weighted DWUI and the equal-metacell DWUI. The omnibus statistic was the maximum absolute standardized weighted PAS difference (each PAS standardized by the square root of the summed squared weighted well differences), and one sign per well was applied to the whole vector and both DWUI differences, testing a zero-centered symmetric well-difference distribution. Up to 18 wells, the sign distribution was enumerated with one sign fixed by symmetry; larger designs used 131,071 sampled patterns with a one-count correction. BH was applied per test and jointly across $3\times268$ tests before intersection with candidates. The five-metric comparison re-extracted equal-metacell vectors for the same 268 genes and 3,566 gene--well records; DWUI, RWUI, PDUI and PPUI used the standardized weighted mean and MPRO the range of aggregated signed differences recomputed for every synchronized sign pattern, with BH per metric (268 tests) and jointly ($5\times268$). Bonferroni-allocated joint 95\% binomial simulation-error bounds for the 215 Monte Carlo tests were propagated through the joint family.

\emph{Conditional count tests.} Every qualified gene--library comparison was tested on its $2\times n$ table of integer PAS counts, with columns zero in both states removed from the test only. Two-column tables used two-sided Fisher exact tests; larger tables used Fisher probability ordering with 131,071 Monte Carlo draws, an identity-derived seed and $P=(1+\#\{\log f(T_{\mathrm{null}})\leq\log f(T_{\mathrm{observed}})\})/131{,}072$. Of 103,830 comparisons, 53,434 were exact and 50,396 Monte Carlo. BH ran within each study--route--contrast--library-pair comparison (92 families of 48--4,930 genes), and simulation-error bounds identified unstable classifications. Count-derived effects were filtered at the metric thresholds and kept separate from equal-metacell effects. These tests assess UMI composition in observed samples and ignore cell-level clustering and overdispersion.
\subsubsection{Public PAS-seq comparison}

GSE99922 PAS-seq\citep{Brumbaugh2018} supplied two untransfected MEF and two iPSC libraries; D3/D6 and Nudt21 perturbation libraries were left out. The 130 mouse counting-rule-consensus genes and 488 mouse P--S genes kept their directions. LastExon coordinates were mapped by GeneID/Ensembl or unambiguous symbol, converted mm9--mm10--mm39 and matched uniquely to same-strand PASs within 50 nt; both coordinate-origin interpretations had to select the same PAS, and overlapping $\pm40$-nt windows, multi-gene sites and many-to-one mappings were excluded. Eligibility required two shared PASs, a 100-bp span, 20 shared counts per library, two sites with ten pooled counts and at least 80\% LastExon count retention per library. Replicates were weighted equally; total variation distance (TVD) was half the absolute sum of the iPSC-minus-MEF mean proportion vector, with MPRO and direction-aligned position changes as separate summaries. Global 1:3 controls excluded all 488 candidates and matched PAS number, count expression/coverage proxies, shared-count fraction, span and pooled usage/concentration; the design required at least 80\% candidate retention and maximum absolute standardized mean difference $\leq0.20$. All six 2-versus-2 label assignments and nine library weightings were reported, so permutation resolution was at best $2/6$. Direct comparisons required at least 80\% common-PAS coverage in both data sets. Because GSE99922 may be represented in the external PAS references, shared site existence counted as nonindependent support.

Expression effects were differences in mean $\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$ among matched APA-eligible metacells, and a study received a GEX direction when all evaluable series agreed in sign with $|\Delta\mathrm{GEX}|\geq0.25$. Study pairs were Guo2019--CIP with Schiebinger2019--2i and Xing2020 with Guan2022. The response-identity null shuffled one study's APA labels ($-1/0/+1$) with the other study's labels and both GEX relationships fixed, within strata of GEX response category, APA-depth tercile, PAS count capped at four, baseline-DWUI quintile and proximal/distal capacity (for multi-series studies, minimum baseline DWUI at least the threshold and maximum at most one minus the threshold); human strata also preserved which Guan2022 series were measurable.
