The direction-only null added a responder indicator, fixing response status and shuffling signs among responders. Each null used 10,000 permutations in both shuffle orientations; the statistic was the number of genes with same-direction APA and opposing GEX, the conservative $P$ was the larger orientation value and enrichment the smaller observed/null ratio. BH covered eight tests (two species, two thresholds, two nulls), and baseline-DWUI terciles formed a separately corrected sensitivity. Spearman correlations among all GEX-opposite genes used continuous APA effects and were descriptive.

Intermediate configurations began with the 488 mouse and 510 human recurrent P--S genes at 0.02 and their directions, a cohort distinct from the Figure~2 candidates. DWUI was computed on the common PAS axes defined above with purity $\geq0.8$, 20 common-axis UMIs per metacell and three metacells with 30 cells per library--state. One documented-source S estimate per gene, route and setting (dates, then units, then libraries equally weighted) was subtracted from the R, E and P estimates, and effects were multiplied by the original P--S sign. Endpoint retention required a P--S estimate in both studies with all evaluable series preserving the direction at 0.02. Process comparisons required S, P and the intermediate state in each designated route: Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i for mouse R/E and Xing2020 and Guan2022--0618 for human R; a Guan2022--0618 R estimate stayed in the background unless the same series had a P--S estimate. At 0.02, paired effects were classified as both aligned with the endpoint, opposite between studies, both reversed, both subthreshold or mixed; directional classes required both effects to reach the threshold, and unavailable estimates were recorded separately. Mouse complete-process summaries used genes with R and E measurable and counted a gene once if either state was opposite; human summaries used R. Sensitivities raised the intermediate threshold to 0.05, required 0.05 at both levels, raised purity to 0.9 or depth to 40 UMIs, used study-native coordinates, or excluded CIP C012 from E and Schiebinger2019--2i L00 from R separately and jointly, rebuilding state values from metacell counts.

An expression-support screen asked whether these study-local states had cross-study expression support. Within each species, it used a 2,000-gene panel excluding highly variable genes and annotation markers, Spearman distances on average-tie ranks of integer metacell counts, batches and time left unaligned, purity $\geq0.8$ and documented-source S. All route-local states competed for the 15 cross-study nearest neighbors. Support required at least nine of the 15 neighbors to carry the same label and the mean distance to the five nearest same-label cross-study neighbors to fall within the 95th percentile (90th as a stricter sensitivity) of the within-study same-state distances, calibrated across libraries where possible. Common-axis DWUI was recomputed within supported metacells with the original weights, keeping the complete-process cohorts (295 mouse, 165 human) and their opposite subsets (60, 51) fixed; missing coverage was never filled with unscreened estimates. The same screen assessed whether endpoint states could support an equivalence-restricted two-study comparison.

Functional analyses used the recurrent sets at $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.02$ by species and contrast. G0 comprised genes detected in both contrasted states in at least two studies; G1, the genes APA-testable in at least two studies, intersected with G0 (excluding one mouse P--S gene, \textit{H2ac19}, and leaving every G2 unchanged); G2 was the recurrent set. Expression summaries averaged nonzero records across libraries within states, across the two states, across series and then across studies. GO biological-process annotations\citep{Ashburner2000GO,GeneOntology2026} used \texttt{go-basic.obo} of 26 July 2026 and Ensembl release 116 mappings\citep{Dyer2025Ensembl,Kinsella2011BioMart}, propagated to ancestors excluding the root. KEGG pathways\citep{Kanehisa2025KEGG} used release 587 (25 September 2026) with REST pathway assignments and Ensembl-to-NCBI conversions. Backgrounds and targets were restricted to annotated genes, and terms with 10--500 background genes were tested by one-sided hypergeometric over-representation (fold enrichment $(h/n)/(K/N)$).

G2/G0, G1/G0 and G2/G1 separated selection stages; G2/G0 and G2/G1 were run for pooled, proximal and distal sets and G1/G0 once, giving 28 analyses per database. Matched tests drew 10,000 gene sets preserving target counts within strata: expression-measurable study count and mean-expression quintile for G2/G0 and G1/G0, and APA-eligible study count (two or at least three) with tertiles of expression, APA coverage, PAS number and reference DWUI for G2/G1. Bins were fixed before annotation filtering, and sampling used annotated background genes with targets allowed in the draws. BH ran within each database, test type and analysis and across each database's 28-analysis grid. Exact tails replaced Monte Carlo estimates for all 102,399 GO and 7,458 KEGG positions: with stratum counts $X_s\sim\mathrm{Hypergeom}(N_s,K_s,n_s)$, convolving the strata gave $P(\sum_sX_s\geq h_{\mathrm{obs}})$. A conditioning ladder recomputed the complete families from the fixed strata: G2/G1 added expression/coverage, reference position and PAS to eligible-study strata (PAS-first as an alternative), and G0 comparisons added expression to measurement count and kept that test thereafter, giving 549,285 exact stage--term probabilities with BH within comparisons, within database/stage and across stages. Conditional power used five terms per comparison chosen by background-size rank (minimum, quartiles, maximum; ties by identifier) and exact noncentral-hypergeometric convolutions at OR=1, 2, 4 and 8; the additional $0.05/m$ threshold ($m$ terms) describes Bonferroni detection.
Cross-species analyses used the ortholog set defined in the joint-embedding methods. Study-specific PAS axes are defined separately for each study and leave homologous PASs unaligned.

Node-based R--S, E--S, P--S and M--S effects required both states to pass the APA filters with at least ten qualified metacells per state and at least two supported PASs spanning at least 200 nt on one chromosome and strand. P--S used library-balanced state means. Paired P--M used the library--state criteria of three metacells and 30 cells, three gene-qualified metacells and two route-supported PASs spanning 200 nt, with effects computed within libraries from raw counts and averaged over sampling units and then sampled times. The two contrasts kept separate measurable backgrounds. Spearman correlations were calculated for each human--mouse study pair among orthologs measurable in both, and state summaries weighted study pairs equally. Direction agreement was the same-sign fraction among orthologs with $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.02$ in both species. Matched P-versus-R/E correlation differences used ortholog-label permutation nulls and BH across a 12-test family including M--S (Supplementary Table~S8a,b). Uncertainty for the equal-pair mean correlations came from 1,000 bootstrap draws of the ortholog union, with each gene's multiplicity shared across study pairs within a state and layer and correlations averaged equally across pairs.

A matched continuous analysis compared validation-species effects between recurrent and non-recurrent genes. Recurrence in the discovery species required two same-direction threshold-crossing studies, with every threshold-crossing study in that direction; orthologs needed an effect in at least two validation studies, aligned to the discovery direction. Comparators had a threshold-crossing effect in at least one discovery study and the same discovery direction and numbers of measurable studies. Controls bracketed each recurrent gene's absolute median discovery effect within a caliper of $\max(0.005,0.25|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}_{\mathrm{discovery}}|)$ (up to ten per side), with linear-interpolation weights equating the weighted control effect; among candidates, selection minimized standardized $\log(1+x)$ distance in supported-PAS number, measurement support, library count and supported span (medians across discovery studies), and controls could be reused. Distinct orthologs were bootstrapped within strata of direction and eligible-study numbers (20,000 draws for the four primary 0.02 analyses, 5,000 otherwise), and $P$ values permuted each ortholog's aligned effect within the same strata with the matching fixed (a discovery-effect-decile restriction as sensitivity). BH covered the four primary and the 30 sensitivity tests separately. Binary and strict replication odds ratios received bootstrap intervals only, and standardized mean differences summarized balance (Supplementary Table~S8d).

\emph{Ortholog-label null.} All 16,092 pairs, including 6,626 unmeasured pairs, were kept as nonmembers in their missingness strata. Ortholog labels were shuffled 5,000 times within study-measurability and supported-PAS strata, with $P=(1+\#\{\text{null}\geq\text{observed}\})/5001$, BH over the two primary tests and a separate 16-test threshold and layer family (Supplementary Table~S8c).

\emph{Node-reference nulls (Figure~4C).} Each species' labels were shuffled independently within strata matching the number of jointly available effect and reference records, supported-PAS terciles and the number of node references with DWUI $\geq0.02$ (a proximal-capacity proxy). Reference DWUI was the observed-S node mean for P--S and the M node mean for P--M, the latter a context proxy for the baseline of the contributing libraries. Q5 added median node-reference quintiles and Range10 separate 0.1-wide bins for minimum and maximum; missing references had their own bins. Each model used 20,000 permutations with BH over its two tests (Table~\ref{tab:core-sensitivity-summary}). These models left expression and coverage unmatched.

\emph{Nested ladder and calibration.} With the 16,092 orthologs and the 18 P--S and ten P--M overlaps fixed, each species' labels were shuffled within strata that successively added contrast-specific measurement count, proximal capacity, reference-position quintile and PAS-count tercile, with a PAS-before-reference path (20,000 draws each). The earlier joint measurement/PAS model was reconstructed by exact convolution and kept outside this ladder. The expected number of assignments to genes lacking proximal capacity, stratum mobility and covariate means were recorded. Calibration generated 3,000 datasets per model; power under the complete model shuffled human labels within strata and drew the mouse overlap from a Fisher noncentral hypergeometric distribution at OR=1, 2, 4 or 8, preserving the margins of every coarser test. Rejection frequencies at 0.05 and 0.025 received exact binomial intervals. Rejection by a coarser test under the complete null indicates sensitivity to omitted conditioning.

\emph{Member tracing.} The 18 P--S and ten P--M members were joined to the global-direction analysis by gene, route, contrast and setting. Support required a proximal effect of at least 0.02 against an eligible positive or negative mean-shift background, evaluated across available and fixed gene sets and the four PAS/purity/metacell settings. Successive flags required supporting studies with positive and negative backgrounds, consistency across that study's other series and source checks, and retention across all four settings; Guan series counted as one study and unavailable series as uninformative. These checks were descriptive.

Sharing between study pairs used documented-source P--S effects (reference-supported layer, purity 0.8) on all jointly measurable orthologs, independently of recurrence. Each of the four pairs combined one human study (Xing2020 or Guan2022) with one mouse study (Guo2019--CIP or Schiebinger2019--2i). Signed labels were $-1$, $+1$ or 0, Guan2022 series had to agree, and orthologs needed measurable effects. Thresholds were 0.02 and 0.05; same-direction sharing summed proximal and distal events. Each side's labels were shuffled within strata preserving the numbers of measurable studies and series and matching expression, APA coverage and PAS-number terciles. The primary model added median source-DWUI quintiles and source-dependent directional capacity; the stricter Range10 model replaced quintiles with 0.1 bins for minimum and maximum source DWUI. Each configuration used 10,000 permutations (base seed 20260927 plus a configuration hash) and $P=(1+\#\{\text{null}\geq\text{observed}\})/10{,}001$. For each model, the eight same-direction tests formed the primary family, 16 directional tests a separate family, and all 24 a broader family. Expected counts were computed analytically from within-stratum label probabilities and checked against permutation means, with movable-label fractions, expected label changes and null variance as diagnostics (Table~\ref{tab:opposite-background-sharing}). The multi-metric version applied RWUI and MPRO labels with the metric-specific strata of the within-species analysis, with families of eight per metric, 24 across metrics and 56 including signed components.

The unit was a one-to-one ortholog with a measurable P--S or paired P--M effect in at least two studies per species. Discovery-active genes had at least one discovery effect with $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq\tau$ and a nonzero median defining direction; the binary outcome was a validation-species median effect of at least $\tau$ in that direction, and discovery recurrence required two supporting studies and zero opposing studies. Five cis predictors described the PASs behind each effect: conserved gain/loss driver-PAS count, conserved discovery-PAS fraction, PAS architecture (twice the matched PAS count divided by the summed human and mouse PAS counts), mean driver phastCons and mean driver motif rank. phastCons used the UCSC mm10 60-way track\citep{Kent2002UCSC,Siepel2005PhastCons}, with hg38 mapped directly and GRCm39 through hg38 to mm10, averaged over $[\mathrm{cut}-100,\mathrm{cut}+50)$; unmapped positions were missing. Reciprocal annotation-based matches within 25 nt defined conserved sites. Conservation and motif rank are sequence predictors.

For each PAS layer, contrast, direction and $\tau$ (0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05), Firth logistic models used a baseline (discovery effect magnitude, eligible-study counts in both species, discovery PAS count), a recurrence model adding the supporting-study fraction, and a full model adding the five cis predictors. The joint cis test compared the full model with a restricted fit with cis coefficients fixed at zero, using a conditional parametric bootstrap of 4,999 outcomes; BH covered the 32 configurations. Imputation, scaling and constant-predictor removal were fitted within training folds of ten repetitions of stratified five-fold cross-validation, and AUC and log-loss changes compared each expanded model with the recurrence model. For the four primary configurations, 2,000 multinomial gene-bootstrap draws kept each gene's out-of-fold predictions across models and repeats to give conditional intervals for the averaged AUC and log-loss differences, excluding refitting and cross-study uncertainty.

Two pools were used, both kept separate from the Figure~1--4 cohorts. The DWUI candidate pool (1,569 mouse and 1,194 human genes) came from a coarse-state registry of genes with same-direction $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|\geq0.01$ in a fixed majority of studies for at least one local-state contrast. A study voted only when every route specified for the contrast was measurable and crossed 0.01 in the same direction: human P--S, M--S and P--M required three of four studies; mouse R--S, E--R, P--E, P--S and P--M both designated studies and M--S two of three. The registry used coarse-state references and Guan2022--0618; missing or conflicting routes abstained and the denominator stayed fixed. These were the only selection criteria. The DWUI--MPRO union, used for Figure~5 and Table~S19, added the MPRO 0.10 recurrence candidates of each P--S or P--M contrast and retained each candidate's selection basis; the two admission rules use unmatched thresholds. Terminal-family counts were available for Guo2019--CIP, Schiebinger2019--2i, Xing2020 and Liu2020.

miRNA site matches were canonical target-side matches to nucleotides 2--8 of mature miRNAs, with names and accessions reconciled to miRBase and MirGeneDB\citep{Kozomara2019miRBase,Fromm2020MirGeneDB}; miRNAs sharing a seed formed one seed-sharing group. The resource retained mature sequences annotated \texttt{functional\_mapped\_rpm>10} in its source bulk small-RNA data (mouse SRP046744; human GSE62776/SRP049345), which indicates expression in those data only. Direct-species RBP position-weight matrices were scanned on the annotated UTR strand with FIMO v5.5.2\citep{Grant2011FIMO} at per-hit $P<10^{-4}$ with resource-specific backgrounds, scanning the forward strand only; transferred mouse motifs formed a separate category. The direct mouse library contained seven scan-ready motifs for six RBPs, compared with 259 motifs for 145 RBPs in human. Union scans covered 1,013 mouse and 1,108 human reference UTR sequences with the same motif banks, duplicate-site rules and overlapping-factor exclusions. Matches are candidate recognition sites.

Each source PAS was matched on chromosome and strand to an integrated-catalog cleavage coordinate within 50 nt, and a unique annotated catalog identity was chosen by source support, nearest distance and deterministic ties. Within each study, gene, terminal family and library--state, counts mapping to the same catalog identity were summed, never across genes or families; families reduced to one PAS were excluded. The annotated PAS coordinate defines the modeled inclusion mask. For union intervals, common UTR boundaries and annotated PAS cuts partitioned each gene into intervals with constant inclusion masks.

For site $i$ in qualified library $\ell$ of state $s$, \[ I_{is\ell}=\frac{\sum_j n_{js\ell}R_{ij}}{\sum_j n_{js\ell}}, \] where $n_{js\ell}$ is the merged count of annotated PAS $j$ in the terminal family and $R_{ij}$ is one when that PAS retains the complete interval; $\Delta I=I_{\mathrm{target}}-I_{\mathrm{reference}}$ in percentage points. Libraries required a terminal-family UMI threshold of 20 or 50 and family coverage $\geq0.5$, where coverage was the family's share of the gene's strict, reference-supported PAS UMIs, and state values averaged qualified libraries equally. A strict inclusion change required same-sign changes of at least 10 pp at both thresholds and at least five included and five excluded UMIs in each compared state at the 50-UMI threshold. P--S used separate-state means because source and target were captured separately, as did the descriptive \textit{Eif4ebp2} profile. P--M used the common qualified libraries $L_{i,k}$ at threshold $k$: \[ \Delta I_{i,\mathrm{P--M},k}=\frac{1}{|L_{i,k}|}\sum_{\ell\in L_{i,k}}\left(I_{i\mathrm{P}\ell,k}-I_{i\mathrm{M}\ell,k}\right), \] with comparisons lacking a common library unavailable; restricting the included/excluded support filter to common libraries was a sensitivity analysis. M was a parallel comparator, and state profiles were projected onto regions after contrast selection.

Physical sites were deduplicated by species, gene, class, chromosome, strand and interval, so each site counted once regardless of compatible factor labels. Site-level cross-study recurrence required matching coordinates and factor, evaluability in both studies and a strict change in the same direction; single-study sites, identity mismatches and non-evaluable sites were kept apart from opposite-direction events. Union interval support required positive physical overlap and the same strict-change direction, deduplicated by gene and contrast.

For direction and magnitude, sites sharing an APA-responsive region were collapsed to matched region pairs. $C_{\mathrm{obs}}$ was the same-direction fraction, $C_0$ the independent-direction reference from each study's positive and negative proportions, and $\Delta C=C_{\mathrm{obs}}-C_0$; $C_0$ ignores the upstream candidate selection. Region effects averaged the 20- and 50-UMI estimates. Intervals for $C_{\mathrm{obs}}$, $\Delta C$ and region Spearman correlations used 5,000 gene-block bootstrap replicates. A magnitude test summarized region effects by gene medians, permuted gene identities 19,999 times (two-sided) and applied BH across the four primary separate-state tests; paired union-pool tests report nominal gene-median $P$ where at least three genes allowed it. A gene-equal sensitivity averaged within-gene agreement and each study's positive-direction fraction over genes before computing $C_0$ and $\Delta C$ (2,000 gene-block draws), and leave-one-gene-out calculations accompanied the correlations. The two-gene human P--M comparison was descriptive.

For the DWUI pool, all 13,985 source-to-catalog mappings were compared with the catalog source and annotated representative, families collapsed to one PAS were identified, and retention masks were recomputed under native-cut and annotated-representative models joined by species, gene, study, site, contrast and threshold. The four displayed intervals (the three Figure~5E motifs and \textit{Hmgn2}) were inspected individually. The state-member sensitivity excluded C012 (provisional) from Guo2019--CIP E and L00 (trajectory-position only) from Schiebinger2019--2i R, rebuilt library-equal inclusion from metacell counts, and recomputed, for each mouse region--route and effect threshold of 5, 10, 15 or 20 pp, the first R/E/P state whose observed-S-referenced change reached the threshold in the endpoint direction at both UMI thresholds, among profiles with complete S/R/E/P support and a qualifying P--S endpoint. This first-crossing label marks the first sampled state past threshold; human labels were unavailable because Xing2020 offered a single R/E subset and R is missing from Liu2020 (Supplementary Table~S15).

Within each Figure~5 gene's shared terminal-structure region, the union of both studies' PAS cuts defined atomic intervals. Changed intervals had same-direction inclusion effects of at least 0.10 in both studies at both thresholds with the included/excluded support; stable blocks combined intervals whose four effects were below 0.05 in magnitude together with upstream constitutive sequence. Each changed interval was matched to an equal-length stable window in the same gene with GC difference $\leq0.05$ and relative-center distance $\leq0.20$, minimizing standardized GC plus position distance; controls could be reused within a gene, and unmatched intervals were reported. Deduplicated direct miRNA/RBP hits fully inside each window were counted once. Changed-minus-control densities per kb were averaged within genes and then equally across genes, with 5,000 gene-bootstrap draws and 10,000 synchronized within-gene sign permutations; BH covered eight species--contrast--category positions, and analyses with fewer than ten genes were descriptive and entered correction as $P=1$. Mature miRNA abundance is unmeasured in the 10x data.
\subsubsection{Candidate context: Rad23b, RBP expression and external resources}

The \textit{Rad23b} seed match came from genome-wide reference seed hits and had to lie inside the common modeled UTR and the shared strict-change interval, belong to the active seed set and be unambiguous at that interval. Prioritization combined cross-study interval support, well-level evidence and published gene function descriptively.

RBP candidates were fixed from Figure~5 relationships with the same physical site and a strict same-direction change in both studies: 122 human and six mouse direct-motif factors and 104 mouse transferred-motif factors, kept as separate classes. Exact case-normalized symbols mapped to one gene identifier in every GEX matrix of Guo2019--CIP, Schiebinger2019--2i, Xing2020 and Liu2020. With purity $\geq0.8$ and library--states of three metacells and 30 cells, metacell CPM was computed from all-gene counts, $\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$ averaged within library--states, and libraries weighted equally. P--S subtracted separately averaged S and P values; P--M averaged within-library differences over common libraries (three, 24, two and one libraries in the four studies). Time-equal weighting averaged libraries within time and then times. An expression flag required count-summed library--state CPM $\geq2$ in at least one qualified library--state, following a developmental APA atlas\citep{Agarwal2021}, and kept every candidate. Figure~5C shows all six mouse direct-motif factors and the six human factors with the most target genes carrying recurrent sites (ties alphabetical), selected before expression was examined. Same-factor sites were deduplicated within gene and contrast, and site-wise inclusion sums were reported at both thresholds unweighted by expression (Table~\ref{tab:rbp-expression}).

Long-read structures for the fixed \textit{Rad23b}, \textit{Hmgn2} and \textit{Eif4ebp2} features came from GSE282319, a reprogramming study of mouse embryonic-stem-cell-derived neural progenitors\citep{Fort2026LongRead}: the filtered GTF, IsoQuant TPM matrix, prefilter SQANTI3 classification, GEO metadata and Supplementary Data~1--2. Coordinates are GRCm39, zero-based and half-open, and UCSC mm39--mm10 chain blocks were accepted only for unique, full-length, same-strand mappings with exact reciprocal return\citep{Kent2002UCSC}. Models had to share the terminal splice boundary, long and proximal pairs had to share complete intron chains, and terminal exons were classified as including, partly overlapping or excluding each feature. Support considered canonical junctions, SQANTI3 RTS\_stage=FALSE and polyA\_motif\_found=TRUE and the published TSS/junction flags, with Ensembl 116 as an additional reference-chain check. The 45 TPM columns are sequencing samples matched to GSM and passage metadata. These checks used processed tables only, leaving BAM/FASTQ reads, poly(A) tails and differential isoform usage unexamined.

For the AGO2 check, the \textit{Rad23b} interval chr4:[55390761,55391176) and seed match chr4:[55390802,55390809) (positive strand) were fixed before retrieving GSE25310-linked tracks\citep{Leung2011Ago2} from the doRiNA archive (\url{https://dorina.mdc-berlin.de/regulators/}), whose metadata assign all five tracks to PMID~21258322: merged WT and merged Dicer-knockout clusters, and WT1A, WT1B and WT2 tracks with knockout clusters removed. Queries were mapped through mm39--mm10--mm9 with unique, same-strand, full-length mappings and exact return; all 415 bases, including the seed target AGCACTT, matched mm9. Overlap required the same chromosome and strand and one shared base, with queries and clusters at their native coordinates. Cluster definitions include 25-nt flanks, so overlap length overstates crosslink coverage. WT1A/WT1B are technical libraries of one preparation (WT1) and WT2 the second biological unit; merged tracks lose replicate membership (Table~\ref{tab:rad23b-ago2}).

In Figures~3D,E and 4E,F, common-weight state means are shown with weighted empirical 10th--90th percentiles of qualified metacell DWUI: each library keeps its summary weight, divided equally among its metacells, and each percentile is the first ordered value whose cumulative weight reaches the requested probability. All 1,587 displayed metacells keep their eligibility rules and PAS weights, and the Xing2020 \textit{RABIF} M group contains three metacells. Lower curves show the fraction of PAS usage distal to each position with the same proportions and weights; their areas divided by the distance-weight span reproduce DWUI (spans 4,039/4,104 nt for \textit{Nudt21} and 2,378/2,287 nt for \textit{Slc38a2} in Guo2019--CIP/Schiebinger2019--2i). The \textit{Slc38a2} library display (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-10}D) keeps all primary qualifying target libraries, including subthreshold comparisons; open markers are unweighted metacell means per library--state, lines pair P and M from one library, dark markers are common-weight summaries, and the single qualified source library per study appears once.

Cell-weighted expression effects for \textit{AP1S2} and \textit{Rtf2} (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-11}D) average each cell's $\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$, zeros included, within metacells and then weight metacells by their cell counts. The displayed $\Delta$GEX is the difference between cell-weighted P and S means, equal to the difference between single-cell means. The corresponding endpoint PAS fractions and study-native documented-source DWUI effects are in Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-11}C. Numerical coverage of the original expression/DWUI projections and the fixed 11 mouse and 7 human P--S examples across 16 routes or series is retained in Table~\ref{tab:supp-revision-data}, including unavailable states and references.

The cross-species state-context display (Table~\ref{tab:supp-revision-data}) projects the 18 P--S and ten P--M orthologs onto the joint embedding. Within each study, metacell DWUI used reference-supported PASs, two supported PASs, an unambiguous strand, a nonzero study-native span and 20 supported UMIs, normalized over the study-native span and centered by the gene's mean across all qualified metacells. For set $k$ in metacell $m$, \[ S_{mk}=-\frac{1}{|G_{mk}|}\sum_{g\in G_{mk}}\left(\mathrm{DWUI}_{mg}-\overline{\mathrm{DWUI}}_{g,\mathrm{study}}\right), \] with $G_{mk}$ the measurable members; the sign is reversed because the selected events are proximal. Scores required at least 6 of 18 P--S or 3 of 10 P--M genes and used one symmetric scale per set, clipped at the 99th percentile. Node-derived and paired effects for the 26-gene union are listed separately (Supplementary Table~S9).

The measurement controls, nested backgrounds, null-result diagnostics, exact functional tails, sequence-background sensitivities, weighted retention, RBP expression and external structure and archive checks were specified after the primary results were known. They are sensitivity and context analyses, kept the primary cohorts fixed and supplement the primary tests. Complete parameter grids, seeds and input hashes accompany the source-data archives, including the null-diagnostics, null-controls and RBP-expression packages dated 20261002.

Reconstructions reproduced the primary estimates before each follow-up analysis. Qualified library--state and route estimates of the six endpoint studies were recovered from integer counts with a maximum absolute discrepancy of $1.72\times10^{-15}$. The multi-metric extraction recovered all 103,830 qualified library pairs and 27,617 gene--route--contrast effects (maximum route-level discrepancy $1.34\times10^{-10}$) and all 48,908 DWUI study--gene--threshold labels. Intermediate-state reconstruction reproduced 23,629 library--state--gene records (maximum discrepancy $9.55\times10^{-11}$). The 1,340 well tests were reconstructed independently from exported vectors, recovering the equal-metacell DWUI $P$ values within $5.55\times10^{-17}$, and every $q=0.05$ classification was unambiguous under the Monte Carlo error bounds. Interval analyses recovered 362,983 mouse and 236,524 human site--contrast records with their paired effects and 11,101 coordinate-region records. Exact functional tails recovered every foreground, background and observed count, and the nine newly supported rows and 24 sampled rows were checked with 70-digit combinatorial probabilities.

Marker expression and program distributions distinguished the reviewed display families while identifying states with residual, mixed or weakly supported programs (Figures~\ref{fig:supp-revised-1} and \ref{fig:supp-revised-2}). Across nine resolution-and-seed perturbations on each of 11 fixed expression graphs, median cell-weighted precision of family assignment exceeded 0.90 in eight expression-analysis subsets and ranged from 0.766 to 1.000, and cluster adjusted Rand indices ranged from 0.465 to 1.000; Guo2019--OSK and Panariello2023 were the most partition-sensitive subsets (Table~\ref{tab:local-partitions}).

The joint embedding preserved broad expression structure more strongly than local neighborhoods. Ten of 12 route pairs exceeded their original-graph held-out-expression null threshold, and eight retained support in all 12 full-atlas refits. Native-versus-joint centroid-distance correlations were 0.900--0.971, whereas equal-library mean 30-neighbor recall was 12.9--20.7\% (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-3}D).
\subsection{PAS measurement and global direction}
\subsubsection{PAS catalog and counting rules}

Sequence context, external-coordinate matches and read-end profiles supported the PAS catalog (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-4}A--D). Among counting-rule changes, enabling atlas PAS affected DWUI most: in the trajectory candidates, study-level 90th percentiles of absolute $\Delta$DWUI differences were 0.024--0.157, whereas other successive changes were usually at or below 0.041 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-4}E). Higher per-metacell UMI thresholds reduced evaluability and produced heavier tails among retained contrasts; for Liu2020 at 80 UMIs the 90th percentile approached 0.37 despite a much smaller median (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-4}F).
\subsubsection{Agreement with alternative PAS callers}

\Reserved{SCAPE-APA/polyApipe comparison: completed scope, site agreement and coverage (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-tool-comparison}A,B), effects on native and common measurement layers with their denominators (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-tool-comparison}C,D), and support for the original recurrent lists (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-tool-comparison}E,F; Table~\ref{tab:pas-caller-comparison}).}

On 710 common orthologs, documented-source P--S contrasts kept opposing directions, with mean $\Delta$DWUI of $+0.03171$, $+0.01985$, $+0.01289$, $-0.01428$ and $-0.02690$ in Xing2020, Guan2022--0618, Guan2022--0809, Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}B). On these study-specific axes, species is confounded with induction, sampling and source differences.

Schiebinger2019--2i was sensitive to which genes became measurable in the expanded primary layer. Its background grew from 2,519 to 2,810 genes and its mean changed from $-0.00655$ to $+0.01116$; on the original 2,519 genes the expanded-layer mean stayed negative ($-0.00564$), whereas the 291 newly measurable genes averaged $+0.15658$. Fixed-background means, medians and proximal-versus-distal event balances remained negative across settings (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}B,C). The documented source also changed the mean while some distribution summaries stayed stable. With fixed target-library pairs (1,912 genes), the two Schiebinger2019--2i D0 sources gave means of $-0.00156$ and $+0.01100$ with proximal medians and event balances. For Guan2022--0618, source and Stage I day 0 references gave $+0.03738$ and $+0.00802$ on 2,899 common genes (the latter median approximately zero), and $+0.03441$ and $-0.00091$ on their own backgrounds (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}D).

On the nucleotide scale of annotation-compatible tandem $3'$ UTRs, route means were $+56.9$, $+63.7$, $+69.2$, $-19.4$ and $-62.2$ nt in Xing2020, Guan2022--0618, Guan2022--0809, Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i (809, 381, 467, 788 and 750 genes; Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}E). Directions held in fixed within-species subsets of 172 human and 222 mouse genes. Requiring compatibility in every route, species and setting left 12 ortholog pairs, among which Guan2022--0618 had a negative mean; weighting by PAS span changes each gene's contribution.

RWUI kept the signs of the five documented-source route means, whereas the endpoint-only PDUI and PPUI kept them inconsistently (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}F). Among genes with at least three supported PASs, DWUI--RWUI Spearman correlations were 0.768--0.819 for P--S and 0.905--0.914 for P--M, and sign agreement among genes exceeding 0.02 in both was 92.68--96.60\% and 99.53--100\%. Redistribution with little net shift was common: MPRO $\geq0.10$ with $|\Delta\mathrm{DWUI}|<0.02$ occurred in 556/2,873 Xing2020 P--S genes, 1,257/3,704 and 1,527/4,877 Guan2022 series genes, 747/2,846 Guo2019--CIP genes and 746/2,326 Schiebinger2019--2i genes with at least three PASs (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}G). Local switching between nearby PASs and compensating changes across the axis can both produce this pattern, as the \textit{COMMD5} and \textit{CNN3} profiles illustrate, each from one qualified source and target library (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-5}H).

The three-class taxonomy remained recognizable under gene subsampling, library reweighting, the expanded primary layer, an alternative seed and route omission (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-6}A--C). Omitting Schiebinger2019--2i, Guo2019--CIP or Xing2020 and projecting the held-out route gave agreements of 0.915, 0.922 and 0.802 (adjusted Rand indices 0.769, 0.781 and 0.507), conditional on the original selection and label matching.

APA scores were organized on expression-only metacell graphs. All 21 study--class combinations showed baseline organization, with median excess Moran's $I$ of 0.672; after state and coverage adjustment the median fell to 0.025 and 11/21 combinations remained significant (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-7}A,B). Fixed-gene panels retained 4/20, 8/21 and 11/21 significant combinations at 70\%, 80\% and 90\% coverage, and neighborhood sizes $k=10$--30 retained 10--16/21 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-7}B).

The C2 transient fraction stayed high as amplitude thresholds increased and in the expanded primary layer, where route medians were 0.733, 0.786 and 0.757 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-6}D--F). S$\rightarrow$R contributed on average 50.6\%, 49.6\% and 39.4\% of C2 path length in Schiebinger2019--2i, Guo2019--CIP and Xing2020, whereas E$\rightarrow$P contributed most to C3 in all three routes, reaching 46.1\% in Xing2020; the most stringent thresholds left smaller subsets.

Monotone profiles with the observed measurement error produced much smaller reversals. The monotone model gave median class $T=0$ in each C2 route, against observed medians of 0.743, 0.813 and 0.757 in Schiebinger2019--2i, Guo2019--CIP and Xing2020. After full-background reselection and reclustering, the middle-endpoint class still had median $T=0$, with 97.5th percentiles of its class-median distribution at 0.241, 0.358 and 0.173 and median class sizes of 12 mouse and 120.5 human genes, compared with observed C2 cohorts of 137 and 165 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-6}G,H). The model leaves systematic state bias unaddressed, and class frequencies describe the selected cohorts only.

APA--GEX correspondence differed across routes, classes and transitions (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-7}C--F). Among 3,888 estimable gene--route profiles, route median Pearson correlations ranged from 0.275 to $-0.144$, and same-sign changes comprised 2,149/4,223 mouse and 2,712/5,816 human adjacent transitions.

Recurrence exceeded reference-DWUI-matched expectations in every species, contrast and threshold (Figure~3A). In human P--M at 0.02, 136 genes had exactly two-study support against a null median of 92 and 34 had three-study support against a median of four; six retained three-study support at 0.05, where the null median was zero (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-8}E). Leaving out each human P--M study preserved aggregate enrichment while changing membership, and treating the two Guan2022 series as separate units kept the direction but reduced the magnitude (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-8}F,G). The recurrent sets retained proximal mouse \textit{Nudt21} P--M and distal human \textit{ANP32E} P--S membership at both thresholds.

The excess persisted under every measurement control (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-8}A,C; Table~\ref{tab:measurement-controls}). With exact series-combination matching, P--S counts of 510/488 compared with null means of 375.18/372.73 (human/mouse) and P--M counts of 170/216 with 97.26/118.65; transformed 95\% excess ranges were 108--161 and 90--141 for P--S and 59--86 and 84--110 for P--M, and all 100 measurable secondary tests had joint 112-position BH values below 0.01. Requiring each bootstrap interval to exclude zero retained 465/510 human and 463/488 mouse P--S members and 108/170 and 192/216 P--M members, with matched counts still above expectation. Twenty-UMI thinning gave 507--530 human and 479--512 mouse P--S genes across 20 draws and 40 UMIs gave 287--301 and 253--268; excess remained at both depths while the cross-study P--S backgrounds shrank from 2,994/1,918 to 1,823/1,084 genes at 40 UMIs. Signed DWUI/depth correlations across the ten route--contrast inventories ranged from $-0.061$ to $+0.130$. Cycle-score matching gave 465 human and 266 mouse P--S genes against 338.38 and 205.69 expected on backgrounds of 2,803 and 1,025, including 426/510 and 214/488 original members; each P--M comparison had at most one study with common cycle support. The common PAS axis gave 584 and 519 against 471.52 and 443.23 on backgrounds of 2,265 and 1,484, and mouse P--M also retained excess. All DWUI follow-up tests had joint $q\leq1.15\times10^{-4}$.

Measurement noise within a state produced little recurrence. Same-state halves gave median S/S counts of 7 versus 367 observed in human and 17 versus 250 in mouse, and P/P counts of 15 versus 283 and 18 versus 293, on identical backgrounds; every observed count exceeded its pseudo-count in all 100 draws (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-8}C). Individual genes could nonetheless cross the thresholds by noise: pooled 95th percentiles of absolute DWUI were 0.0265/0.0378 (S/S, P/P) in human and 0.0399/0.0406 in mouse, and MPRO 95th percentiles were 0.0856--0.1225. The halves have reduced depth and capture measurement and within-state variation only.

The excess persisted under detailed background conditioning. All 40 positions of the nested within-species ladder retained BH support at the 10,000-draw floor (about $q=10^{-4}$); at 0.02 the complete-model expectations were 375.15/372.64 for P--S and 97.05/118.65 for P--M (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-8}D). Complete-model nulls rejected 3.7\%--5.1\% of simulated datasets, and a shared log-weight standard deviation of 0.5 added on average 32.46 human and 36.87 mouse P--S recurrent genes and was detected in 78.2\%/88.3\% of replicates.

Recurrence held under all six counting rules (Table~\ref{tab:core-sensitivity-summary}; Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-8}B). All 48 species--threshold--view--rule tests reached $P=q\leq1.0\times10^{-4}$ within their families. At 0.02 in the fixed-gene view, the original rule gave 396 human and 319 mouse recurrent genes, unrestricted transferred windows 296 and 302 (retaining 172 and 182 original-view members) and full-atlas clipping 314 and 275 (182 and 169). Consensus across rules was itself more frequent than its joint null: 132 human and 130 mouse genes in the fixed-gene view and 146 and 139 with common contributors at 0.02, and 51/55 and 52/58 at 0.05, all above their null maxima. Of the fixed-gene members, 128 human and all 130 mouse genes matched the unrestricted list in identity and direction (139 and 135 with common contributors), and none reversed an original direction.

Alternative summaries also recurred. All RWUI and MPRO configurations exceeded metric-specific expectations, including under the 24-test correction across three metrics (all $q\leq0.000200$; Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-10}A). At 0.02, RWUI gave 601/646 human/mouse P--S and 155/233 P--M recurrent genes; at MPRO 0.10, counts were 1,893/1,376 and 149/232, but P--S enrichment was only 1.063/1.045, and MPRO recurrence allows different directions or PAS changes across studies.

Individual membership was less stable than the aggregate. On the common axis, 289/510 human and 327/488 mouse original identities and directions were retained. In Schiebinger2019--2i wells, all 62 testable members of the 216-gene mouse P--M cohort had same-direction equal-metacell DWUI support and 60 also reached 0.02; the other 154 had insufficient coverage. Across the 268-gene well background (4--11 dates with duplicated wells, 8--22 wells per gene), joint BH supported 195 PAS-vector omnibus, 192 count-DWUI and 189 equal-metacell DWUI tests. In the five-metric family, DWUI and MPRO shared 171 supported genes, with 15 supported only by DWUI and 14 only by MPRO (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-9}A,B); joint BH supported 186 DWUI, 189 RWUI, 46 PDUI, 45 PPUI and 185 MPRO tests (189/194/29/25/192 in separate families). Among 266 genes with at least three PASs, DWUI and MPRO support covered 184 and 183 genes, and effect thresholds retained 93 DWUI ($|\Delta|\geq0.02$) and 81 MPRO ($\geq0.10$) genes. Of the 62 covered candidates, 62 had DWUI and 61 MPRO support. \textit{Tomm20} had a small proximal DWUI effect of $-0.01434$ (joint $q=0.000238$) with proximal effects in all 22 wells across 11 dates, but MPRO of 0.02456 ($q=0.05780$). Among the 14 MPRO-only genes, only \textit{Aopep} exceeded MPRO 0.10 (0.1457, $q=0.0341$; DWUI 0.00183, $q=0.3424$), and 11 of the 15 DWUI-only genes had MPRO $q$ between 0.05 and 0.10 (Table~\ref{tab:metric-candidate-significance}).

Source-referenced well inference was weaker. P--S covered 927 genes, with 155 count-DWUI and 152 equal-metacell DWUI tests supported; 27 and 37 of these had zero variance between the two source wells, leaving 128 and 115 with nonzero source variance (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-9}D). Of the 488 mouse P--S candidates, 211 were covered: 53 retained direction, $q<0.05$ and the 0.02 effect, three changed direction and 155 had $q\geq0.05$, while coverage was insufficient for 277 (42 retained with nonzero source variance; Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-9}F). This estimate combines state, date and medium.

Other designs had too coarse a resolution for corrected discovery. Panariello2023 P--M retained 1,006 genes with four (93), five (415) or six (498) pools; unadjusted $P<0.05$ occurred for 175 DWUI, 185 RWUI, 40 PDUI, 31 PPUI and 150 MPRO tests, all with six pools, but none passed BH. Even if every gene reached its minimum two-sided sign-test $P$, the best metric-specific BH value would be 0.06313; the observed joint minimum was 0.2501 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-9}E). Conditional count tests supported 80,057 of 103,830 gene--library comparisons at $q<0.05$ with simultaneous Monte Carlo upper bounds and 80,141 with point estimates, and simulation error spanned the decision threshold for 188 comparisons; these describe UMI composition within observed samples.

Public PAS-seq gave limited external support (Table~\ref{tab:sequence-background-external}B). Strict measurement was available for 49/130 counting-rule-consensus genes and 133/488 P--S genes. Primary 1:3 matching retained 38/49 (77.6\%) consensus genes, below the 80\% design criterion, and 108/133 (81.2\%) P--S genes, with maximum absolute standardized differences of 0.132 and 0.121. Candidate-minus-control mean TVD differences were 0.87 and 0.38 pp (0.14--1.58 and 0.15--0.80 pp across nine library weightings), and the four libraries allow only six label assignments (minimum unsigned probability $2/6$). Direct common-PAS comparisons covered 20/130 and 6/130 consensus genes in Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i, whose position effects agreed with external iPSC--MEF in 19/20 and 5/6 genes (Spearman 0.516 and 0.200); for the P--S set, coverage was 56/488 and 19/488, agreement 42/56 and 13/19 and correlations 0.441 and 0.275. Both comparisons reuse the same four external libraries and overlapping genes, and none of the four example genes met the direct-comparison criteria.

About half of the P--M recurrent genes also met the criterion against the documented source. Complete source--within-library comparisons were available for 1,111 genes in Xing2020, 2,050 in Guo2019--CIP and 867 in Schiebinger2019--2i (752 in both mouse studies). Within the recurrent cohorts, 200/216 mouse and 146/170 human genes had complete measurements; all 200 mouse and 125 human genes kept the P--M criterion, and 97 and 78 also met it in P--S (in both mouse studies, or within Xing2020). The 97 mouse members comprised 91 proximal and six distal responses, and their M--S responses were aligned in both studies for 20, opposed in both for 15, subthreshold in both for 13 and mixed for 49; the 78 human members comprised 30 proximal and 48 distal responses. Dual-reference membership therefore marks P relative to two references, which falls short of a P-exclusive response. Coverage changed membership while the connection persisted: purity 0.9 retained 93/197 mouse and 76/146 human members, the expanded layer 104/203 and 80/146, and five metacells in every P/M/S group 64/135 and 11/26. The mouse sets under these three settings kept 92, 94 and 60 of the original 97, and 57 belonged to all four; at 0.05, 43 mouse and 38 human members met the stronger criterion. The \textit{Slc38a2} display retained 268 metacells and seven target libraries, and all 24 documented-source metacells in Schiebinger2019--2i had DWUI of 1 on its axis (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-10}D).

MPRO and DWUI selected different candidates (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-10}A,B; Table~\ref{tab:metric-candidate-differences}). At MPRO 0.10 versus DWUI 0.02, recurrence-defined additions comprised 1,450 human and 930 mouse P--S genes and 70 human and 82 mouse P--M genes. \textit{Mtpn} belonged to both P--M recurrence sets but had DWUI-only well support, and \textit{Fam3c} had MPRO-only recurrence and DWUI-only well support. Many additions also responded relative to the source (Table~\ref{tab:matched-state-metrics}A). Of 82 mouse MPRO-only candidates, 74 were measurable with common P/M/S contributors in both studies; all kept P--M MPRO $\geq0.10$ and 60 also reached it in P--S in both studies. Of 66 mouse DWUI-only candidates, 58 were complete and 43 had P--S MPRO responses in both studies, although none met the two-study P--M MPRO criterion. In Xing2020, 58 of 70 MPRO-only candidates were complete, 47 reached the P--S threshold and 45 both P-state contrasts. \textit{Nudt21} illustrates the dependence on summary and coverage (Table~\ref{tab:matched-state-metrics}B): with identical PASs and contributors, P--S DWUI effects were $-0.0194$/\allowbreak$-0.0167$ and MPRO 0.0404/0.4630 in Guo2019--CIP/\allowbreak Schiebinger2019--2i. Requiring five metacells per state kept the Schiebinger2019--2i P--S MPRO response at 0.1935, with P--S DWUI of $-0.0219$ and P--M MPRO of 0.0809, while Guo2019--CIP was unchanged.

Recurrent APA also occurred in genes whose expression changed in opposite directions: 65 and 39 mouse genes and 78 and 49 human genes at 0.02 and 0.05 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-11}A,B). Under the response-identity null, human enrichment had $q=0.0032$ and 0.0308 and mouse $q=0.0834$ and 0.1037. Under the direction-only null, which fixes responder status, human $q$ values were 0.0627 and 0.1718 and mouse 0.1718 and 0.5780, none passing the eight-test correction; with baseline terciles in place of quintiles, the human 0.02 direction-only test gave $q=0.0451$ (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-11}A). Using continuous effects, correspondence among all GEX-opposite genes was modest (Spearman $\rho=0.142$ in mouse and 0.210 in human). \textit{Rtf2} had opposing cell-weighted P--S expression effects of $+1.03$ and $-1.00$ in Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i with recurrent proximal APA (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-11}D). \textit{AP1S2} had expression effects of $-1.22$ in Xing2020 and $+3.53$ in Guan2022--0809 with DWUI effects of $-0.531$ and $-0.475$, and $-0.430$ in Guan2022--0618 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-11}C,D and Table~\ref{tab:supp-revision-data}). This expression-context cohort is distinct from the dual-reference cohort, although both human summaries contain 78 genes.

Intermediate states of recurrent P--S genes showed heterogeneous configurations (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-12}A). Of the 488 mouse and 510 human genes, 418 and 415 had measurable endpoints on the common axes, and 307 and 261 retained direction and the 0.02 effect; endpoints were unavailable for 70 and 95 genes and a further 111 and 154 lost the direction or the 0.02 effect. Paired intermediate measurements among retained genes covered mouse R (302), mouse E (298) and human R (165); 86 retained human genes had a Guan2022--0618 R estimate unpaired with a same-series P--S contrast and stayed in the background. Opposite configurations occurred in 47/302 mouse R, 33/298 mouse E and 51/165 human R comparisons, and 60/295 genes in the complete mouse R/E intersection were opposite in at least one state (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-12}B,C). Raising only the intermediate threshold to 0.05 retained 32/295 mouse and 27/165 human genes, and the 0.05-endpoint/0.05-intermediate subset contained 24/191 and 21/106 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-12}D). Jointly excluding CIP C012 and Schiebinger2019--2i L00 retained 59/291, and 40 PAS UMIs gave 32/143 and 16/79 with reduced coverage; purity and study-native axes likewise retained opposite configurations.

Cross-study expression support for these study-local states was sparse and state dependent. Under the 95th-percentile criterion, supported S/R/E/P metacells numbered 0/79, 58/454, 74/704 and 75/85 in Guo2019--CIP and 52/84, 5/1,139, 1/334 and 492/571 in Schiebinger2019--2i; human S/R/P counts were 33/130, 0/59 and 32/46 in Xing2020 and 61/177, 1/681 and 0/145 in Guan2022--0618 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-12}E). Different criteria removed each set: label agreement excluded all Guo2019--CIP S metacells, the distance criterion excluded Guan2022--0618 P metacells despite their P-labeled neighbors, and Xing2020 R had too few calibration neighbors and favored S. Under both the 95th- and the 90th-percentile screens, complete source--intermediate--endpoint measurements were lost for all 295 mouse and 165 human genes (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-12}E), so the configurations remain study-local. The same screen gave limited endpoint support: human M support was 0/130 in Xing2020 and 0/433 in Guan2022--0618 and mouse M support 194/329 and 153/360, so complete two-study P--S and human M comparisons were unavailable for screening. Cycle-matched P--M was likewise unavailable, because common-bin support was absent in Guo2019--CIP and panel scores were unavailable for Liu2020/Panariello2023.

Two recurrent genes have reported roles relevant to reprogramming. \textit{CDKN1A} met the directional P--M criterion with DWUI effects of $-0.0247$/\allowbreak$-0.0326$ in Liu2020/\allowbreak Panariello2023 and MPRO of 0.0493/\allowbreak 0.0675, below 0.10 in both (Table~\ref{tab:metric-candidate-differences}); it encodes p21 in a pathway that limits reprogramming\citep{Hong2009p21}. \textit{Fam3c} met the MPRO 0.10 criterion with opposing P--M net directions ($-0.0400/+0.0259$ in Guo2019--CIP/Schiebinger2019--2i); FAM3C/ILEI promotes epithelial--mesenchymal transition in mammary epithelial and breast cancer models, and hnRNP E1 regulates its translation through the $3'$ UTR\citep{Woosley2019ILEI}. Effects of these PAS changes on protein output remain untested.

Gene-set associations depended mainly on the background (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-13}A,B; Table~\ref{tab:exact-functional}). Conventional over-representation highlighted RNA processing, translation, protein handling and trafficking; mouse P--S KEGG terms included protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum, ribosome, protein export and spliceosome. Across the 28 analyses per database, conventional tests gave 1,014 significant GO and 116 KEGG comparison-level rows, repeated across comparisons. Covariate matching with 10,000 draws gave no term with $q<0.05$, whereas exact tails of the same matched distributions recovered six GO and three KEGG comparison-level rows. Five GO rows described APA testability (G1/G0); the sixth was mouse P--S proximal ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis relative to expressed genes (G2/G0; $q=0.0422$). In mouse P--M proximal G2/G1, integrated stress response signaling and the lipid and atherosclerosis annotation each had $q=0.0342$. Across each database's full grid, only human P--S G1/G0 intracellular protein transport remained supported ($q=0.0238$), whereas the G2 rows had $q_{\mathrm{grid}}=0.1567$--0.5032. Pathway labels describe annotation overlap.

The conditioning ladder showed that expression and coverage matching removed most conventional associations, with little further change from PAS or baseline matching (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-13}C,D). For GO G2/G1, the smallest within-comparison $q$ was 0.167--0.323 across stages, including the stage that omitted reference position and PAS number. Expression/coverage adjustment reduced GO G2/G0 supported positions from 66 to one and G1/G0 from 913 to five, and KEGG from 14 to one and 101 to zero; these counts are comparison--term positions. The two KEGG G2/G1 rows appeared only under complete conditioning, so finer conditioning can also strengthen a term-specific association. In the term-size-selected G2/G1 panel, OR=2 had median nominal detection probabilities of 19.0\% (GO) and 18.1\% (KEGG), and 0.10\% and 0.37\% at the Bonferroni term-family threshold, so modest associations would usually be missed.

Human and mouse effects corresponded little. Among orthologs with strong effects in both species, direction agreement was 49.1\%, 51.3\% and 48.5\% for R--S, E--S and P--S on state-specific backgrounds (Supplementary Table~S8a), and the matched comparison of P--S correspondence with R--S, E--S or M--S had a smallest $q_{12}$ of 0.210 (Supplementary Table~S8b). Equal-pair mean correlations were $-0.016$, 0.015 and 0.020 for R--S, E--S and P--S, with ortholog-block bootstrap intervals of $-0.040$ to 0.007, $-0.025$ to 0.054 and $-0.007$ to 0.047; P--S study-pair correlations ranged from $-0.060$ to 0.082, six of eight positive (Figure~4B and \ref{fig:supp-revised-14}A). These small, narrowly bounded estimates leave little room for a large common continuous association hidden by multiplicity correction. None of the 30 estimable direction-aligned continuous comparisons passed correction, and residual matching imbalance was largest for P--M (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-14}D; Supplementary Table~S8d). Among 755 direction-concordant and 777 direction-discordant strong R/E records, corrected association with discordance was absent for library, metacell, PAS-support, within-node variability or cross-layer stability measures (Supplementary Table~S8e); repeated records per gene and study limit this check.

Support for the shared proximal sets depended on the null. Under the ortholog-label null that matched observability and PAS count, P--S sharing passed the 16-test sensitivity correction only at 0.02 in both PAS layers and paired P--M at 0.01--0.03 in both layers, and at 0.05 had $q_{16}=0.301$ (P--S) and 0.080 (P--M) in both layers (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-15}C; Supplementary Table~S8c). Under the node-reference nulls, the 18-member P--S overlap stayed within expectation ($q=0.1482$ for Q5 and 0.1848 for Range10), whereas the ten-member P--M overlap retained support ($q=0.0038$ and 0.0045; Figure~4C; Table~\ref{tab:core-sensitivity-summary}).

The nested ladder located the P--S change in baseline position (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-15}D; Table~\ref{tab:null-controls}). With orthologs and the shuffle mechanism fixed, the P--S expectation rose from 12.42 with measurement-count matching to 12.61 with capacity, 13.76 with baseline position and 13.90 with PAS number, against 18 observed ($P=0.0680$, 0.0768, 0.1477 and 0.1499); adding PAS before baseline gave 13.11 ($P=0.1020$). P--M kept support throughout, with ten overlaps against 2.68--3.47 expected ($P=0.00025$--0.00185). Measurement-only shuffling placed on average 9.45 human and 17.54 mouse P--S events on genes lacking proximal capacity in two studies, which capacity conditioning removed. The earlier jointly stratified P--S result used a different reference distribution and lies outside this ladder. In 3,000 complete-model datasets with zero added association, the P--S capacity-only test rejected 10.5\% and the complete test 4.0\%; the complete test detected OR=2, 4 and 8 with probabilities of 68.0\%, 99.7\% and 100\% in P--S and 17.0\%, 57.7\% and 86.0\% in P--M, whose null rejection rate of 2.0\% reflects discreteness (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-15}E). This trade-off between omitted-condition sensitivity and power leaves open whether baseline and PAS properties carry biological as well as technical variation.

Member tracing linked the shared sets to opposite mean-shift backgrounds with membership fixed (Figure~4D). Of the 18 P--S members, 15 kept support across opposite backgrounds, nine also passed documented-source and series checks, and eight kept support in all four settings: \textit{BUB3}, \textit{DLAT}, \textit{ETFRF1}, \textit{H1-0}, \textit{HSPD1}, \textit{RAB1A}, \textit{SRPRA} and \textit{SZRD1} (human symbols). \textit{M6PR} passed the series check, but one opposite Guan2022--0809 record in the expanded layer removed it from the all-setting set. Of the ten P--M members, six passed the first two checks and four all settings. A traced member could still be subthreshold, opposite or unavailable in another study, and the study-state matrix is shown in Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-16}.

Stronger responses were shared in selected study pairs (Table~\ref{tab:opposite-background-sharing}). At 0.05 under the primary model, Xing2020/Guo2019--CIP shared 130 events against 105.43 expected ($q=0.0056$ in the eight-test family), and Guan2022/Guo2019--CIP and Guan2022/Schiebinger2019--2i shared 106 and 95. Range10 retained the first two ($q=0.0264$ and 0.0104), whereas the third had $q=0.0622$; Xing2020/Schiebinger2019--2i had $q_8=0.3193$ and 0.4581 under the two models, and at 0.02 the smallest $q_8$ was 0.0604. Under the exploratory within-DWUI 24-test family, the three pairs had $q=0.0168$/0.0528, 0.0341/0.0300 and 0.0341/0.1171 (primary/Range10). Shared sets contained both directions: 50 proximal and 80 distal members for Xing2020/Guo2019--CIP and 59 and 47 for Guan2022/Guo2019--CIP. Backgrounds of 1,309--2,098 orthologs kept positive human and negative mouse route means (for Xing2020/Guo2019--CIP, $+0.03676$ and $-0.00879$); the Xing2020 and Guan2022 comparisons share Guo2019--CIP and are therefore dependent.

Sharing was more metric-dependent than within-species recurrence (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-15}A,B). No primary RWUI or MPRO test reached within-metric $q<0.05$ (minima 0.373 and 0.0808), although all nulls had nonzero variance; in the reconstructed DWUI comparison, three stronger-threshold pairs passed the eight-test family, only Xing2020/Guo2019--CIP passed the 24 primary tests across metrics ($q=0.0264$), and no test passed the 56-test family including signed components (minimum $q=0.0616$). Four DWUI, zero RWUI and two MPRO primary positions had unadjusted $P<0.05$. Exchangeability also varied: at 0.02, about 92\% of genes on each side of Xing2020/Guo2019--CIP could change labels (87\% under Range10), whereas for Guan2022/Guo2019--CIP at 0.05 under Range10, about 40\% of human genes were movable and 14\% changed labels per permutation. Across 48 saved nulls, simulated and analytical means differed by at most 2.63 Monte Carlo standard errors.

Within species, P--S recurrence occurred on same-sign mean backgrounds, but human P--M recurrence crossed opposite ones: 69/170 recurrent genes at 0.02 and 23/59 at 0.05 had same-direction support across the positive Liu2020 and negative Panariello2023 mean backgrounds, a contrast specific to means, absent from medians and event balances. Back-projection of the 26 shared proximal orthologs assigned P--S scores to 79--99\% and P--M scores to 83--98\% of displayed cells across six studies, with study-specific measurement coverage (Table~\ref{tab:supp-revision-data}).

Cis features gave small and uncertain predictive gains (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-17}). In the primary mouse-to-human P--S analysis ($\tau=0.02$, reference-supported layer; 723 genes, 145 positive outcomes), adding the five cis predictors increased mean cross-validated AUC by 0.0324 (conditional gene-bootstrap interval $-0.0023$ to 0.0673) and reduced log loss by 0.0036 ($-0.0065$ to 0.0138); AUC improved in 10/10 and log loss in 8/10 repetitions, which reuse genes. Both P--M directions lost discrimination ($-0.0294$ and $-0.0695$, with 30/191 and 20/195 positive outcomes), and mouse-to-human P--M log loss increased by 0.0276 (0.0102--0.0469; Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-17}D). Two nonprimary configurations passed the 32-test correction: P--S mouse-to-human at $\tau=0.03$ ($n=618$, 88 positives; $P=0.0028$, $q=0.0448$) and P--M human-to-mouse at $\tau=0.05$ ($n=84$, nine positives; $P=0.0004$, $q=0.0128$; Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-17}C).

The DWUI--MPRO union contained shared same-direction strict inclusion changes at 3,576 miRNA-compatible and 1,513 RBP-compatible physical sites in mouse and 519 and 525 in human, with region-pair counts and gene denominators in Table~S19; the inventory and partial-retention summaries used paired P--M estimates from common libraries. Restricting the included/excluded support filter to common libraries left the cross-study inventories unchanged and altered single-study fractions by at most 0.18 pp. MPRO recurrence added 562 mouse and 1,127 human P--S gene--contrast candidates and 58 mouse and 57 human P--M candidates beyond the DWUI pool. Of these, 208/303 mouse/human P--S and 30/20 P--M genes were evaluable in both Figure~5 studies, and 17/15 and 5/1 had shared same-direction strict changes (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-18}C). These counts differ from the recurrence-defined additions above because the DWUI pool used a different selection rule.

\textit{Rad23b} entered as a recurrence-defined addition. Its study-native P--M MPRO was 0.1755 and 0.3411 and DWUI $-0.00466$ and $-0.04223$ in Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i, and in the matched-well analysis both MPRO (0.2835, $q=0.0341$) and DWUI ($q=0.0194$) were supported. On the annotated terminal-family axis, the shared interval chr4:[55,390,761,55,391,176) decreased in paired P--M inclusion by 11.48/19.37 pp at 20 UMIs and 11.48/20.12 pp at 50 UMIs, with 3/24 and 3/22 common libraries. A reference match at chr4:[55,390,802,55,390,809) (zero-based GRCm39) was compatible with seed AAGTGCT, shared by miR-291a-3p, miR-294-3p, miR-295-3p and miR-302a/b/d-3p. Structural review excluded other leads: \textit{Fxr1} kept P--M MPRO of 0.2635/0.3103 at 20 UMIs, but its modeled UTR structures shared only a 1-nt variable interval, and an eligible terminal-family model was unavailable for \textit{Aopep}.
\subsubsection{The DWUI pool, paired estimates and audits}

In the DWUI pool, recurrent matched region pairs across P--S and P--M comprised 134 pairs from 56 mouse genes and 31 pairs from 22 human genes (Tables~S10--S15). After deduplication across contrasts, exact cross-study partial recurrence comprised 98 miRNA and 80 RBP gene--factor relationships in mouse and 30 and 42 in human (Table~\ref{tab:supp-revision-data}), distinct from the single-study fractions in Supplementary Table~S12. Requiring common physical libraries affected P--M more than P--S: the paired estimator retained 75/94 mouse matched regions from 25/39 genes but only 4/31 human regions from one of 21 genes, and both paired sets had direction agreement and marginal expectations of one, giving zero excess (Table~\ref{tab:core-sensitivity-summary}). Human gene-block uncertainty and magnitude inference were unavailable, so the separate-state human P--M inventories remain descriptive.

The coordinate audit found 57 of 13,985 mappings whose annotated representative lay more than 50 nt from the source PAS and 113 families collapsed to one PAS. Among 1,438,533 shared site--contrast--threshold records, 80,983 changed structural class and 13,618 changed strict-change status between native-cut and annotated-representative models. None of the four displayed intervals changed class, and one \textit{Hmgn2} S--R threshold classification changed with its E--P effects unchanged. The reconstructed Liu2020 E state was measurable for all 31 human regions at 20 UMIs and 27 at 50, whereas R remained unavailable (Supplementary Table~S14). The state-member sensitivity changed 57 of 1,072 mouse first-crossing labels and none of the eight \textit{Hmgn2} labels, leaving its S/P/M profiles unchanged (Table~\ref{tab:supp-revision-data}; Supplementary Table~S15). At \textit{Hmgn2}, inclusion of the miR-23a/b-3p-compatible interval fell from E to P by 24.5 pp in Guo2019--CIP and 32.7 pp in Schiebinger2019--2i (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-21}A,C), and seven of ten selected loci showed exact cross-study partial recurrence; the other three were \textit{Usp3}, \textit{FBXW7} and \textit{SPARC} (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-21}G).

Interval direction agreement depended on weighting. Equal gene weights raised the human P--S excess from the region-weighted 11.8 pp to 18.9 pp (95\% gene-block interval 4.8--31.6), whereas mouse P--S stayed positive at 11.6 pp (3.4--19.9). Mouse P--M stayed at zero because all 85 pairs decreased and both marginal directions were saturated. The three eligible region-effect correlation intervals still included zero, and the two-gene human P--M comparison was too small for a reliable interval.

Matching attrition limited the density comparison. The 44 human and 121 mouse P--S changed intervals yielded 12 and 35 matched windows; the unmatched intervals (human/mouse) were lost at the stable-sequence (14/22), equal-length (7/23), GC (3/13) and position (8/28) steps (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-19}C). Under strict matching (25 mouse and ten human P--S genes), changed-minus-stable mean densities were $-8.76$ and $+13.77$ sites/kb for miRNA and $-0.73$ and $-0.40$ for direct RBP motifs, and none of the four P--S tests passed correction ($q=0.902$--1); P--M retained nine mouse and one human gene and was descriptive (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-19}A,B; Table~\ref{tab:sequence-background-external}A).

Relaxed matching increased coverage and left the null result unchanged. Removing GC and position limits raised matched genes from 10 to 18 in human P--S, 25 to 37 in mouse P--S and nine to 18 in mouse P--M, while human P--M stayed at one. Human P--S miRNA differences stayed positive across the 12 settings (6.23--13.77 sites/kb) and mouse values negative ($-10.00$ to $-4.72$), with unrestricted-matching intervals of $-5.41$ to 20.07 and $-22.15$ to 2.43 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-19}D). No setting had unadjusted $P<0.05$ (minimum 0.0625), and all 96 BH values were 1. The mouse P--S RBP comparison had 25 genes but only three nonzero differences, all negative (exact two-sided $P=0.25$), and its direct library covered six RBPs, so it applies to these six RBPs and is unsuited to comparison with human. The transferred-motif category was also unsupported (all $q=1$; minimum $P=0.0898$), with mouse P--S differences of 3.43 sites/kb ($-5.92$ to 14.88) under strict and $-0.66$ ($-7.70$ to 6.12) under unrestricted matching. Motif-independent window selection and cross-gene donors (ten human and 25 mouse P--S, one human and nine mouse P--M genes) stayed above nominal significance across six backgrounds (minimum $P=0.0551$, for lower mouse P--S miRNA density under the cross-gene GC/position background; all 48-position $q=1$).

The density tests had low power for moderate or sparse effects (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-19}E). Adding 10 sites/kb to every P--S gene was detected in 8.7\% of human and 20.4\% of mouse simulations and 20 sites/kb in 25.7\% and 58.6\%; restricting the 20-sites/kb shift to about a quarter of genes gave 6.1\% and 7.8\%. Dense injections create nonzero differences in genes that originally had zero differences, so power for the sparse mouse direct-RBP results remains uncertain.

Site retention changed with interval usage independently of local density. Strictly changed human P--S, mouse P--S and mouse P--M intervals contained 455, 1,859 and 2,206 miRNA-compatible sites, and their usage-weighted sums were $+75.64$, $-253.67$ and $-417.63$ at the 20-support layer, with the same signs at 50 (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-18}A,B). Among genes with sites, 19 of 29 human P--S genes had positive and ten negative net changes, mouse P--S had 13 positive and 43 negative genes, and all 30 mouse P--M genes were negative. This scan cohort is separate from the union inventory and included unmatched intervals.
\subsubsection{Candidate RBP expression}

Expression distinguished otherwise similar motif candidates (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-20}; Table~\ref{tab:rbp-expression}). Across 4,872 metacells, 99 of 122 human direct-motif candidates reached 2 CPM in at least one qualified state in Xing2020 and 106 in Liu2020 (98 in both, 15 below threshold in both), and all six mouse direct-motif candidates were expressed in both studies; the 104 mouse transferred-motif candidates kept their designation. For P--S, \textit{Rbm38} increased by 2.73 and 2.40 units of mean $\log_2(\mathrm{CPM}+1)$ in Guo2019--CIP and Schiebinger2019--2i and \textit{RBM38} by 1.56 and 3.68 in Xing2020 and Liu2020. Mouse \textit{Pcbp1} increased in both contrasts, including P--M changes of 0.56 and 1.12, whereas human \textit{PCBP1} had opposing P--S changes ($-0.61$ and $+0.69$) despite concordant P--M increases. \textit{ELAVL2}, ranked first by recurrent target-gene count, stayed below 2 CPM in every qualified Xing2020 state, with mean P-state library CPM of 0.38 versus 9.54 in Liu2020. Of 119 human factors with recurrent P--S sites, 93 had endpoint expression support in both studies, of which 53 increased in both, 13 decreased in both and 27 diverged; for P--M, 44 of 59 factors had support, with 24, nine and eleven, respectively. Time-equal weighting changed the sign class of one human direct-motif P--S candidate, \textit{ZC3H12B}, whose effects were near zero, whereas all mouse candidates kept their class. Expression and retention could diverge: the eight mouse genes with shared P--S-changing \textit{Rbm38}-compatible sites showed reduced inclusion while \textit{Rbm38} increased, and the two human target genes showed increased inclusion. These descriptive effects leave an RBP's functional sign, protein abundance and binding to direct tests.
\subsubsection{External transcript structures and the AGO2 archive}

Public long-read models supported the inclusion/exclusion structure at the three fixed loci (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-21}E,F and \ref{fig:supp-revised-22}B; Table~\ref{tab:external-long-read}). The filtered GSE282319 annotation contained 48 \textit{Rad23b}, 20 \textit{Hmgn2} and eight \textit{Eif4ebp2} models. \textit{Rad23b}.G35551.3 and G35551.79 shared nine introns and were jointly detected at TPM $\geq1$ in 37 of 45 sample columns; the longer terminal exon included the 415-nt interval and seed, and the proximal exon retained the first interval base but excluded all seven seed bases. G35551.111, detected in five samples, excluded the whole interval. \textit{Hmgn2}.G37326.164/G37326.203 shared their chain and included or excluded the miR-23-compatible site (joint detection in 29 samples); both carry non-coding predictions, so they support RNA structure only. \textit{Eif4ebp2}.G4810.13/G4810.21 shared their chain and retained or excluded both variable Pcbp1-compatible motifs (29 samples), and G4810.74 (14 samples) also excluded motif~1, which is therefore constitutive only within the modeled PAS family. These structures come from neural-progenitor reprogramming and inform structure, leaving the direction of fibroblast P--M usage to the single-cell data.

The AGO2 archive was uninformative about seed-specific binding at \textit{Rad23b} (Figure~\ref{fig:supp-revised-22}C; Table~\ref{tab:rad23b-ago2}). Merged WT and Dicer-knockout tracks each overlapped 145 bp of the interval, beginning at chr4:55391031, 222 nt beyond the end of the seed. The three WT library tracks with knockout clusters removed lay outside the interval, so WT1A/WT1B and WT2 supplied zero overlapping biological units in that filtered archive. The interval association is shared with the knockout archive and separate from the seed; it leaves both miRNA-dependent binding of the seed and AGO2 binding in the original experiments unresolved.
